450	
451	**PF-34. Unseen lies and no leak culling.**
452	*Rule.* A listed lie is drawn whenever its surface is on screen and lit; there is no "seat away" special case; its trajectory is a function of sim time and reappears at the correct point. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP; Sanity now lists away entries, SN-23 `away`)* Sanity keeps an entry listed while the seat is in another compartment (`away` true), so a lie seen through an open door, from a hatch or at a zoomed-out field is one continuous lie: no ONSET, no RETURN, no CLEAR, no sound OFF or new ON, and no change to `amp`, `leak_modes`, wander or breath when the seat crosses a hatch. A RETURN begun by a compartment change would give the test "walk out of the room; if the gauge settles it was lying", an end-of-lie signature that PF-G9 and SNV-11 forbid. S3 state and the RETURN follower of a ref that is off screen advance on elapsed `present_time` by scalar arithmetic (no draw or shader work; the follower closes min(gap, R_ret x elapsed)), so a lie that ended while its surface was off screen is, when next drawn, exactly where an on-screen return would have put it (finished unless seen inside its return window); on the first drawn frame after an off-screen interval the ONSET/HOLD slew is re-latched with `hard_start` (D.3) so it equals the formula. At far zoom (the large field) level-of-detail may reduce amplitude *detail* (breath sampling rate only; the wander amplitude and frequency are never reduced, D.4), never remove a leak mode. Counts are bounded by `LIES_MAX`, not by the field, so zooming out multiplies nothing.
453	*Why.* "A culled leak is an unleaked lie" (OQ-SN-17 answered; SN-15 L-L). (orchestrator ruling R17.)

337	
338	**SN-23. The perception content contract and the first frame.**
339	*Rule.* `sanity.perception` lists, per seat: `stage`, active lies `{lie_id, slot, subject_ref, kind, direction, reach_tier, params, start_run, active_run, end_run, leak_modes, first_lie, away}` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: `away` added, G6 GAP)* as typed in the entry schema below (SN-16 lie timing; `leak_modes` always contains GLEAM and the motion bit, SN-15 L-L) and, VS-A, phantom, hide and lure lists. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: the entry is now a closed schema, see **Entry schema**.)*
340	
341	**Entry schema (closed; every field is `int`, `bool` or `String`; the Filter reads nothing else).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING; answers Perception Filter OQ-PF-35 and OQ-PF-38 items 1, 2 and 4.)* The `sanity.perception` entry list is in **ascending `slot` order** and holds at most `LIES_MAX[stage]` entries per seat:
342	
343	| field | type | definition |
344	|---|---|---|
345	| `lie_id` | int >= 1 | minted at the accept from the persisted ledger counter `next_lie_id` (per seat, starts 1, +1 per accept; it is not a draw counter and advances no RNG stream); stable for the life of the lie including its Filter RETURN tail, never reused in a world |
346	| `slot` | int 0 to `LIES_MAX[3]` - 1 | the lowest free slot at the accept among the seat's live (PENDING or ACTIVE) lies, held until the lie ends; ties impossible (one accept per run per subject, processed in the SN-16 order) |
347	| `subject_ref` | `{stable_id: String, surface: int}` | `stable_id` is the module's Item/Layout stable id; `surface` is the `lie_targets.json` surface-kind enum, a closed set owned here: 1 NEEDLE, 2 READOUT, 3 GLYPH, 4 GLOW_SPRITE, 5 MACHINE_SPRITE. The inspect card is **not** a separate surface and not a second entry: it is the same instrument as its wall gauge (SN-16 reach, AD-C1), so the Filter draws the card from the NEEDLE or READOUT entry. No WORN-descriptor surface is listed at the MVP (no `PerceptionRef` exists for it, Perception Filter PF-9) |
348	| `kind` | int enum | 1 FALSE_OK, 2 FALSE_FAIL, 3 GLIDE, 4 SPRITE_SWAP (registry `lie_kinds`) |
349	| `direction` | int enum | 1 COMFORT, 2 ALARM (L-D), as stored at the accept; immutable for a `lie_id` while the lie lives (a re-derivation that disagrees INVALIDATES it, SN-16); the Filter latches its GLIDE side from it (Perception Filter D.3) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, answers Perception Filter blocker 2)* |
350	| `reach_tier` | int 1 to 3 | the lowest stage at which the surface is legal (NEEDLE and READOUT 1, GLYPH and GLOW_SPRITE 2, MACHINE_SPRITE 3), derived from `surface`, so the Filter never re-derives reach |
351	| `params` | Dictionary, closed key set per kind | FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL and GLIDE on a NEEDLE or GLYPH: `{}` (a GLYPH, GLOW_SPRITE or static MACHINE_SPRITE carries no motion param: the Filter draws BREATH, or the rotor drift, from `surface`, PF-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; on a READOUT: `{readout_mode: int}` (1 TICK, 2 STALE; the numeral's motion mode, Instruments C2), defined as a pure function of the kind: GLIDE gives 1 TICK, FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL give 2 STALE (Perception Filter PF-18); it consumes no draw (the draw count per accepted onset stays 4, SN-24); a NEEDLE entry's card numeral follows the same map without a param *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, answers Perception Filter blocker 2)*; SPRITE_SWAP: `{frame_id: String}` (the machine's own honest alternate frame). Values are `int`, `bool` or `String` only; a `float`, `Vector2`/`Vector2i`, `Node`, `Object`, `Callable`, nested Dictionary or Array is a lint failure (`SANITY_BOOT_LIE_TARGET_DATA` for the data file, AC-SN-136 at runtime) |
352	| `start_run`, `active_run`, `end_run` | int | absolute `run = T div 12` (SN-1 units), `active_run` published (OQ-PF-17), `end_run` counted from activation |
353	| `leak_modes` | int bitmask | non-empty, GLEAM (1) and bit 2, the surface class's motion mode (L-L), always set *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* |
354	| `first_lie` | bool | true on the entry accepted while `lies_seen` was 0 |
355	| `away` | bool | true iff the subject's compartment (the Graph cid holding the module's anchor node) differs from `cid(P)` at this run, else false; a pure function of ledger and `cid(P)`, rebuilt every run and in `post_restore`; read only by the `reach_lie_active` predicate and the Filter's rim gate *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP, supersedes the 2026-10-27 delegated G1 listing rule)* |
356	
357	**Which entries are listed.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP, supersedes the 2026-10-27 delegated G1 listing rule.)* Every ACTIVE entry of the seat is listed, whichever compartment its subject sits in; entries whose subject is not in `cid(P)` carry `away` true. An away entry keeps its clock, its `lie_id` and its slot, and leaves `sanity.perception` only on a real end (EXPIRED, DEBUNKED, INVALIDATED), identical to an entry the seat is standing beside. PENDING entries are not listed. The `stage` field is always listed. Reason: a removal on leaving would make the Filter run its RETURN on every lie visible through an open door or at far zoom, a reliable "walk out of the room; if the gauge settles it was lying" test and an end-of-lie signature (SNV-11); the Filter must not be able to distinguish an away flip from nothing, and it draws only surfaces that are on screen and lit. This closes OQ-SN-17 (and Perception Filter's "away entry" question) on the Sanity side. The fringe oracle is closed by the predicate, not by hiding the entry. **Reach-lie predicate (OQ-SN-21):** `reach_lie_active(P)` is true iff the seat's `stage >= 2` and a **listed** entry with `away` false and `reach_tier == 2` has stepped PENDING to ACTIVE (a PENDING lie is not listed at all); the Filter evaluates it on the listed entries only, so it is a pure function of `sanity.perception`. Away entries and `reach_tier` 3 entries never drive the fringe. **Diagnostic accessor** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, Debug Overlay blocker 1)*: `ledger_listed(player_id, lie_id) -> bool` is true iff `sanity.perception` for that seat holds an entry with that `lie_id` in the current Sanity run, i.e. the row is ACTIVE (away or not); false for PENDING rows, ended rows and an unknown id. It is a pure function of SIM state, derived (not persisted, not a ledger field, not in the SHAPE key set, no `schema_version` change, not hashed), rebuilt in the same hook step that rebuilds `sanity.perception` (SN-2 step 6, after the state transitions and the `cid(P)` evaluation, so the two always agree) and in `post_restore`. The only permitted reader is the Debug Overlay (DIAGNOSTIC); no sim system reads it. An away row is listed, so the Filter holds an entry for it and the Overlay's join sees no skew. **Leak mask:** Sanity stores the full `leak_modes` mask in the ledger; the Filter's plausibility drop of the SOUND bit at stages 2 and 3 (PF-15) is a pure `rng_derive` keyed `"filter.leak/<PlayerId>/<lie_id>"` (the Filter's stream name, a proposed registry stream) that advances no counter and touches no ledger field, so the SIM state is identical with the Filter on or off, and the published mask is never reduced below two modes (L-L). **Legal-kind additions (OQ-PF-38 item 3).** The SN-16 legal-kind set, before `sum_W`, also removes a kind whose pre-draw eligibility fails for the Filter: (a) the subject's dial leaves less than `D_VIS_MIN_DEG` plus the wander margin of room on the side of the lie's `direction` (the dial-room gate) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, answers Perception Filter blocker 2: was "in some direction")*: for a GLIDE the room is measured on the dial side `s = d x c_dial` (`d` +1 COMFORT, -1 ALARM; `c_dial = sgn(mid(OK) - mid(A))` from the authored OK and alarm intervals of the subject's `lie_targets.json` row, the rule of Perception Filter D.3), so a GLIDE whose only room is the wrong way is refused without a draw; for FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL gate (b) already covers the zone side; (b) for FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL, the zone-edge distance plus `m_z` exceeds `D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000` (the zone-edge gate); both read the Filter's registered constants and the **authored** dial range and zone intervals in `lie_targets.json` for the subject's true-state class (HEALTHY, DEGRADED, FAILED, which Sanity already reads from `hp`), never `true_value()` (the Interactions row keeps that read the Filter's alone), and both are no-draw gates (a refusal advances nothing). They are a provisional contract until the Filter confirms the constants (R9); the Filter's `lie_short_reach` and `lies_zone_missed` counters remain the safety net. It states **WHAT and WHEN**, never HOW (no pixels, shaders, alphas, easing). Every entry carries a non-empty leak (SN-15 L-L). It is rebuilt **in full** every run and in `post_restore` (CR-8: `persist false` means derived, rebuilt after load). Lint: no symbol of `sanity.perception` or `sanity.ledger` is read outside `sanity/` except, respectively, the Perception Filter / replication adapter and the Debug Overlay (DIAGNOSTIC); `ledger_listed` is read only by the Debug Overlay (DIAGNOSTIC) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. H5 (KRN:125) and CR-12 assert it. `post_restore` rebuilds from the restored `sanity.state` and `sanity.ledger` (`restore_after` places the ledger after the Graph and Layout blocks so subject refs resolve, SL-15 item 8); a **malformed** ref, or any out-of-range or wrong-shape value, is a hard `SANITY_RESTORE_*` failure and is never clamped. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review, BLOCKING: a well-formed `subject_ref` that no longer resolves is **not** corruption and is not a failure. Sanity runs only when `T mod 12 = 0` while Save/Load snapshots at any tick boundary (SL:453), so a subject destroyed or salvaged between hook runs and followed by an autosave leaves a legitimate dead ref in a valid save; the MVP death rule (restart from the last autosave) would otherwise hard-fail on it. `post_restore` therefore does three things and mutates nothing persisted: it restores the ledger exactly as stored; it builds `sanity.perception` from the ledger **exactly as the uninterrupted run holds it at that tick**, the dead-ref entry included, so the projection stays field-for-field equal (the Filter draws nothing for a subject that no longer exists, and an unresolved ref answers like unlit, EM-21); and the next hook run's ledger-upkeep step (SN-2 step 4) INVALIDATES the entry with no immunity and prunes its `visit`, `evented[]`, `debounce[]`, `immune[]` and `repaired_recent[]` entries, exactly what the uninterrupted run does. Pruning inside `post_restore` is rejected because `state_hash` would then differ between a restored and an uninterrupted run for up to 11 ticks, which breaks AC-SN-76's every-tick equality. Sanity has no destruction callback and none is requested of the Graph or Layout.)*
358	*Why.* This answers SL H4, "no clean frame": one unfiltered frame would be a free oracle. Sanity claims **co-ownership of SL OQ-11 with the Perception Filter and the Pipeline** (C9) and states its half: the perception data is ready before the first RUNNING frame (AC-SL-93).
359	*Edge notes.* The soft cycle Sanity to Filter (IDX:267) resolves by one-way ownership: Sanity writes only perception state; the Filter writes only `CanvasItem` and material properties and never calls back. The Filter's per-stage onset smoothing is its own, subject to PR-13 (at most 3 flashes in a rolling 1 s) and "no uncaused pixel motion". **Ended entries are not retained** (Perception Filter OQ-PF-9): an ended lie leaves `sanity.perception` on the same run (SN-16), so loading clears the Filter's presentation-local glide-return tail; the first RUNNING frame after a restore shows the true value behind the black hold with no lie active to hide, so it is not a clean-frame oracle, and the residual is accepted.

259:**PF-8. The `Perceived` record.**
276:**PF-9. `PerceptionRef`.**
351:**PF-18. Lying readouts: tick, stale-hold and card parity.**
394:**PF-23. The own-cone rim fringe (MVP-conditional).**
463:**PF-37. Presentation randomness.**

259	**PF-8. The `Perceived` record.**
260	
261	| Field | Type and range | Meaning |
262	|---|---|---|
263	| `displayed_pm` | int 0 to 1000 | the value the needle, readout or glyph shows, as per mille of the instrument's range; wander included; equals the true reading on the honest path |
264	| `displayed_value` | number in the unit of `true_value` for the ref | the same value in the ref's own unit, for numerals and suit keys (derived through the PF-45 calibration); equals `true_value` on the honest path |
265	| `frame_override` | StringName or NONE | the honest state frame to show (SPRITE_SWAP, glow sprite, glyph); NONE on the honest path. For SPRITE_SWAP the frame is `params.frame_id` (Sanity's honest alternate frame); the Filter picks no frame, and PF-19's "one of the machine's own honest state frames" stays true because Sanity's `frame_id` is one *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)* |
266	| `motion_mode` | HONEST, GLIDE, TICK, STALE, BREATH, RETURN | HONEST: Instruments apply settle and tremor. GLIDE: Filter-owned trajectory, no settle. TICK: the readout ticks continuously. STALE: the readout is held. The "readout" is the card numeral (and any digit readout), i.e. the `displayed_value` of the ref's record: TICK and STALE govern that numeral only, and the needle of the same ref draws `displayed_pm`, always with the never-rest wander, in every non-HONEST mode (Instruments C2, OQ-IW-19). BREATH *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a static-pair frame (housing, glyph, machine state) is showing its false state and its gleam breathes between `floor_eff` (D.5) and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s, the hue-independent mode of that surface class (PF-15 table, D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. RETURN: the lie ended and the follower closes the gap; the mode stays RETURN until CLEAR (PF-12, D.5) |
267	| `tick_phase_ms` | int | ms since the last digit change (TICK only) |
268	| `leak_amplitude_pm` | int 0 to 1000 | the gleam amplitude at this instant (PF-15, D.5); gleam only; the sound level is the separate unbreathed `amp_snd` on the audio request *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1/R8)* |
269	| `leak_modes` | bitmask {GLEAM = 1, GLIDE = 2, SOUND = 4} | modes in force after the drop rule; always contains GLEAM and the motion mode (PF-15); bit 2 (named GLIDE, Sanity's "motion bit") stands for the surface class's hue-independent motion mode: needle drift and wander, TICK or STALE, BREATH, or rotor drift *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
270	| `tremor_weight_pm` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int 0 to 1000 | the share of an honest tremor already in progress that Instruments may still apply: 1000 on the honest path; on a lie's first ACTIVE frame it falls linearly to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (:= `WANDER_ONSET_S`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, so a gauge that was trembling at onset blends out instead of stopping dead (the onset rule of PF-17). It never starts a tremor, and a lie never borrows one |
271	| `lie_id` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int, 0 = none | the lie handle, for logs and the Debug Overlay: Sanity's `lie_id` verbatim (minted per seat at the accept, >= 1, never reused; SN-23) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`)*, so it is non-zero for exactly as long as a lie is ACTIVE or in RETURN and 0 on the honest path. It is kept (with `lie_kind`) through RETURN and becomes 0 (`lie_kind` NONE) only at CLEAR (S3 `NONE`) (OQ-DO-2 (v)). The Debug Overlay's `lie_id != 0` discriminator (DO-21) and its join by (viewer, subject_ref) are unchanged |
272	| `lie_kind` | FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL, GLIDE, SPRITE_SWAP, NONE | echo of Sanity's kind |
273	
274	*Rule.* The record **never contains the true value** when a lie is active; it is what the seat *perceives*. A remote `viewer` returns the honest record (PF-10). *Why.* A record that carried the truth beside the lie would hand the HUD a way to leak it. The record is a request to Instruments and the HUD, not their design.
275	
276	**PF-9. `PerceptionRef`.**
277	*Rule.* The ref is a tagged union: `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)`, `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` (the `quantity` term, one of the Instruments IW-9 quantities, keeps two compartment instruments in one room distinct in the PF-7 memo and selects the `true_value` kind; K-5, OQ-IW-26), `SUIT_KEY(key)` (the five keys `suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge`), `SCANNER`, `HOUSING_GLOW(ref)`, `STATE_GLYPH(ref)`, `MACHINE_FRAME(ref)`. The inspect card uses the **same ref** as the wall gauge it mirrors: there is no separate card ref and no separate lie. A ref resolves to Sanity's `subject_ref` through the tag's `lie_surface_id` plus the Graph id *(provisional — the Graph-node-to-subject mapping is the one named assumption of SN-16's lit-entry rule, routed to Interaction and Derelict Authoring)*. A stable integer `ref_key` (kind, id and, for a compartment, `quantity`; never an instance id) feeds the hash (PF-37).
278	*Why.* One union, one wrap point (orchestrator ruling D11). Suit rail counts are not keys (SE OQ-6) and stay anchors.
279	**The join: Sanity's `subject_ref` to a `PerceptionRef`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)*. Each row of the Sanity-owned `lie_targets.json` is a pair (module kind, surface kind) and each ledger `subject_ref` is the published pair `{stable_id: String, surface: int}` (surface 1 NEEDLE, 2 READOUT, 3 GLYPH, 4 GLOW_SPRITE, 5 MACHINE_SPRITE; SN-23). `quantity` is NOT part of the key: a compartment gauge is its own instrument with its own `stable_id` (IW-8 `instrument_id`), so two gauges in one room are two keys; the `quantity`, node id or `cid` are read by the constructor from the instrument record found by `stable_id` (`lie_targets.json` row plus IW-8 record) and feed the `PerceptionRef` and `ref_key`, never the join. The Filter resolves it with exactly one constructor, so a lie can never attach to two refs and a ref can never receive two lies from one entry (AC-PF-112 tests the bijection on every row).
280	
281	| Sanity `surface` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity's closed schema)* | IW-8 facet of `lie_surface_id` | `PerceptionRef` built from the record | True source (read only by the Filter) |
282	|---|---|---|---|
283	| 1 NEEDLE | `<instrument_id>.needle` | `GRAPH_NODE(kind, id)` or `GRAPH_COMPARTMENT(cid, quantity)` per the record's `node_ref` / `room_key` / `quantity` (wall gauge and card share this ref, HR-14) | Graph `true_value` |
284	| 2 READOUT | `.needle` of a `gauge_kind` READOUT instrument | same constructor | Graph `true_value` |
285	| 3 GLYPH | `.glyph` | `STATE_GLYPH(GRAPH_NODE)` | the node's state |
286	| 4 GLOW_SPRITE | `.housing_glow` | `HOUSING_GLOW(GRAPH_NODE of the lamp)` | appearance frame only (the light and `lux` stay TRUTH) |
287	| 5 MACHINE_SPRITE | `.machine_frame` | `MACHINE_FRAME(GRAPH_NODE)` | the node's state, both honest frames required |
288	
289	`SUIT_KEY`, `SCANNER` and WORN have no `surface` value at MVP (honest paths; Sanity lists none; WORN stays VS-A with no ref type, PF-5 row 21, out of the MVP coverage lint, PF-6 vi; `SCANNER` has no published true source, OQ-PF-36). A listed `surface` outside 1 to 5, or one that does not match the record's `gauge_kind`, draws nothing and counts `lie_unrenderable`. The inspect card is not a surface (it is drawn from the NEEDLE or READOUT ref, HR-14), matching Sanity. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*
290	
291	**PF-10. Per-viewer scope.**
292	*Rule.* The Filter answers for the **local seat only**. A remote PlayerId passed to `perceived` returns the honest record (counter `remote_queries`); it is never an error. Addressing is by PlayerId, never `peer_id`. `sanity.perception` is `OWNER_PRIVATE`; the replicated `SHARED_SUMMARY` `{stage, tell_on, harm_eligible}` is what lets viewer A draw seat B's tell fringe (VS-B).
293	*Why.* Answering a remote PlayerId from replicated data would let a client compute another's lies (SN-26). (orchestrator ruling R9.)
294	
295	#### B. The lie: clock, trajectory, leak, end
296	
297	**PF-11. Lie clock and purity.**
298	*Rule.* A lie's trajectory runs on **sim time**, clocked from the lie's **activation run**: `lie_tau = (T_c - SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR * act_run + tick_alpha) / TICK_RATE`, with `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` 12 (registered; equal to the kernel hook divisor by relation, not a knob), `TICK_RATE` 60, `act_run` the run on which the entry became ACTIVE, clamped at 0 (D.1). Pause freezes the tick and therefore the lie. Presentation phases that carry no information (wander phase, breath phase, tick cadence) run on `present_time` (PIPE PR-9). The displayed value is a **pure function of the entry, the live true value, `lie_tau` and per-lie constants, modulo PRESENTATION-local state**: the single slew state of PF-13 and PF-14, which is never persisted and is rebuilt from the formula on `hard_start` (PF-33). While a lie is ACTIVE its displayed value is the formula's value, so a restore reproduces it **up to the slew gap that was still closing at the save** (D.3, PF-33) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the per-lie constants (rate, magnitude, wander frequency and phase, tick stagger and sign, sound-breath period) are restore-exact because their hash key is the saved `lie_id` (in the saved ledger, with its counter `next_lie_id`), and `epoch` is 0 for every per-lie draw (D.14); the GLIDE direction and the numeral mode are not hash draws but published entry fields (`direction`, `params.readout_mode`; PF-13, PF-18), saved with the entry *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Sanity publishes `lie_id`, `direction`, `readout_mode`)*. `start_run` and `active_run` are used for the clock only.
299	*Why.* A trajectory on `present_time` would restart from phase 0 after a restore and show a different displayed value (breaking PF-33); a trajectory on sim time is restore-exact and pause-consistent. A lie is a moving value of the world, so it is interpolated with `tick_alpha` (PIPE PR-8 rule 5), not an animation (rule 6): the world moved, so the lie must have advanced. The clock starts at **activation**, not at the accept: Sanity stamps `start_run` at the accept (SN-16, EC-SN-29) and activates `ONSET_DELAY_RUNS` (10 to 25 runs, 2 to 5 s) later, so a clock from `start_run` would put the first ACTIVE frame 2 to 5 s into the glide, a first-frame jump of up to 10 deg that PF-13 and SNV-13 forbid.
300	Sanity publishes `active_run` in the perception entry (registry `sanity.perception`); `act_run` is that field.

631	## Formulas
632	
633	*Conventions.* Every formula below is a **presentation** computation. Nothing here is hashed into `state_hash`, replicated or persisted (KERN D.12 excludes the perceived channel), so the kernel's integer-only determinism rule does not bind D.1 to D.13 and D.15 to D.17, which use floating point on the render thread. **D.14 is the one integer-only formula**: its outputs must reproduce across builds and platforms and are pinned by test vectors (AC-PF-30). Angles are degrees on the instrument's dial arc `arc_deg`; dial readings are per mille (`pm`) of the instrument's range, `pm = deg x 1000 / arc_deg`; pixel measures are art px of the 640x360 grid (`n` art px is `n x k` screen px at ladder step `k`). Time is either **sim time** (`T_c`, the last committed tick count, plus `tick_alpha`, KERN D.3) or **`present_time`** (PIPE PR-9, frozen while PAUSED); each formula says which. `[PLACEHOLDER]` marks a number invented here (range and registered-name proposal in Tuning Knobs); a name followed by "(cited)" is owned elsewhere and used at its registry value. The numbering D.1 to D.17 is the one the rules cite: PF-11 D.1, PF-13 D.2 and D.3, PF-17 D.4, PF-15 D.5, PF-14 D.6, PF-21 D.7, PF-30 D.8, PF-18 D.9, PF-31 D.10, PF-32 D.11, PF-42 D.12, D.13 CPU, PF-37 D.14, PF-20 D.15, PF-35 D.16, PF-19 D.17. Dependency formulas are referenced by name, never restated: KERN D.3 `tick_alpha`, KERN D.10 `rng_derive` (sim-only, never called here), KERN D.12 `state_hash`, PIPE D.15 `flash_count`, PIPE D.16 `D_BUDGET`, LO-22 (including `flash_governor`), SN D.5 (onset). GDScript integer overflow semantics, `Dictionary` ordering and per-call costs are not sourceable (there is no `scripting.md` or `core.md` in `docs/engine-reference/godot/`); every place that depends on them is marked `[UNV]`.
634	
635	### D.1 Lie clock
636	
637	The lie clock formula (registry: `lie_displayed_value`; covers D.1 to D.4) is defined as:
638	
639	`lie_tau = max(0, (T_c - SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR * act_run + tick_alpha) / TICK_RATE)`
640	
641	`first_frame_discrepancy_bound_deg = GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG * (n_f + 1) / TICK_RATE`
642	
643	**Variables:**
644	
645	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
646	|---|---|---|---|---|
647	| `T_c` | int | 0 to 2^53 | KERN tick counter | last committed tick; presentation reads it and never writes |
648	| `SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` | int | 12 (cited, registered; equal to the kernel hook divisor by relation, not a knob) | Sanity | ticks per sanity run |
649	| `act_run` | int | >= 0 | `sanity.perception` entry (`active_run` = `start_run` + delay_runs, published by Sanity; registry `sanity.perception`) | the run on which the entry became ACTIVE. Sanity stamps `start_run` at the accept and activates `ONSET_DELAY_RUNS` (10 to 25 runs) later, so `start_run` is **not** the origin. |
650	| `tick_alpha` | float | [0, 1] | KERN D.3 (cited) | interpolation fraction inside the current tick |
651	| `TICK_RATE` | int | 60 (cited) | Command & Simulation Layer | ticks per second |
652	| `n_f` | int | 1 to 2 | measured | ticks that elapse per rendered frame (1 at 60 fps, 2 at the 30 fps floor) |
653	| `lie_tau` | float s | 0 to about 120.2 | derived | seconds since activation; the upper end is the `LIE_LIFE_S` maximum (120 s, Sanity) plus one run and one frame |
654	| `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` | float deg/s | 2.0 (named here, value from ART 7.3) | art bible | the fastest drift |
655	
656	**Output Range:** `lie_tau` is 0 at activation and clamped at 0 when a restore or a `force_stage` makes `act_run x 12 > T_c`. It is frozen while PAUSED (the tick and `tick_alpha` are frozen). It is unbounded above only if Sanity fails to remove an expired entry. **First-frame bound:** the first rendered frame sees the entry at most one frame after its hook tick, so `lie_tau <= (n_f + 1) / TICK_RATE` and the displayed-minus-true discrepancy on the first ACTIVE frame is at most `2.0 x 3 / 60 = 0.1 deg` at the 30 fps floor (0.067 deg at 60 fps), which is below `LEAK_EPS_DEG` 0.25 deg: the first frame carries no visible departure (AC-PF-45 tests "below `LEAK_EPS_DEG`", not "exactly zero"). If the Sanity hook's phase offset is not 0, `act_run x 12` is up to 11 ticks (0.18 s) early; the error is constant per lie and invisible.
657	
658	**Example:** `act_run` 1000, `T_c` 12300, `tick_alpha` 0.5: `lie_tau = (12300 - 12000 + 0.5) / 60 = 5.008 s`. A restore that lands with `T_c` 11990 gives `(11990 - 12000 + 0) / 60 < 0`, clamped to 0. While PAUSED for 30 s `T_c` and `tick_alpha` do not move, so `lie_tau` stays 5.008 s.
659	
660	### D.2 Glide parameters (rate and magnitude, drawn once per lie)
661	
662	The glide parameters formula is defined as:
663	
664	`rate_draw = GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG + (GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG - GLIDE_RATE_MIN_DEG) * (h_rate mod 1001) / 1000`
665

(3) The slew is invisible whenever the target's per-frame change is within `R_act x dt`, which is always true for the formula itself (its own drift is at most `rate <= GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` and `R_act` is that bound). (4) The slew becomes visible only after a **step in the true value** (a Graph step, `apply_damage`) or a **lie hand-off** (a new lie starting while a return is in flight, E-PF-3); it then reconverges in at most `gap / R_act` seconds, at most `0.5 x 1000 / 8.33 = 60 s` for a half-dial step before the cap, and never leaves `DISC_CAP_PM` of the truth (so the worst lag is about `DISC_CAP_PM / R_act` = 48 s; typically a few seconds) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The tip is drawn at an integer art-px position (nearest sampling) and moves along the needle's tangent, so its rounded position is the pair of two rounded axis positions and it changes when either axis's rounded coordinate changes. Per axis the tip is a sinusoid of amplitude `A m_i` (`m_x = abs(cos phi_n)`, `m_y = abs(sin phi_n)`) about an offset `c_i`, the fractional pixel position of the held target. One axis stays on one pixel longest in the unit-wide level band that sits at the sinusoid's peak with its lower edge exactly at the mean, a fraction `acos(1 - 1/(A m_i)) / pi` of the period, so its dwell is `acos(1 - 1/(A m_i)) / (pi f)`. The pair rests only while both axes rest; the worst case aligns both bands on the same peak, and the dwell is then that of the axis with the *larger* amplitude, `m = max(m_x, m_y)`, which is smallest and so worst at 45 degrees (`m = 1/sqrt(2)`). At `A` 2.0 and 0.35 Hz the single-axis dwell is 0.952 s but the 45-degree dwell is **1.158 s**, over the 1.0 s ceiling, and no amplitude inside the old range (1.85 to 2.5) could fix it (it needs 2.59 px at 0.35 Hz); at `A` 2.2 and `WANDER_F_MIN` 0.40 the dwell is **0.959 s at 45 degrees** (0.791 s at 0 and 90 degrees), a margin of 4 %. A brute-force model over a 24 x 24 grid of fractional offsets and needle angles 0 to 90 degrees in 15-degree steps agrees with the analytic bound to 0.02 s (0.942 s measured at 45 degrees; 0.998 s against 1.001 s analytic at `A` 2.0 and 0.405 Hz, the smallest frequency that would have fixed the old amplitude). The proof is for a **single sinusoid**: the two-sine sum (0.6 and 0.4 weights) proposed in a specialist draft has a beat envelope that falls to 0.2 of its peak, in which the rounded tip rests for the length of a beat, so it is not adopted. Under reduced motion the wander is **not scaled** (PF-39), so `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` does not touch the bound. **Onset (measured, bounded):** during ONSET the drift moves the tip at least 0.5 art px per second by `rate_floor` (tip speed `v = needle_len_px x rate x pi / 180`: 0.50 px/s at 24 px and 1.19 deg/s) and the wander fades in linearly over `WANDER_ONSET_S`; the worst-case rest from the first ACTIVE frame, over needle angle, phase and fractional pixel and with no credit for the drift, is **1.15 s** at 0.40 Hz (1.04 s at 0.45 Hz), inside the stated bound `ONSET_REST_MAX_S` = `WANDER_ONSET_S + NEVER_REST_MAX_S` = 2.0 s (AC-PF-46). A lie whose truth sits at a dial stop (`lie_short_reach`) keeps the full wander, because the target clamp leaves the wander margin `W_M` (D.3), and relies on it as its motion mode.

Peak tip speed at 0.45 Hz is `2 pi x 0.45 x 2.2 = 6.22 px/s`, which is 14.9 deg/s angular on a 24-px needle: far above the 0.5 to 2 deg/s band, which is why the band is read as the drift component only (CONFLICT C-1). With hash `H(1, 0x1234, 7, 0)`: `h_wf mod 1001` = 467 gives `f_w = 0.40 + 0.05 x 0.467 = 0.4234 Hz` and `phi_w = 2 pi x 0.105 = 0.66 rad`; the worst-case dwell at 0.4234 Hz is `acos(1 - 1/1.556) / (pi x 0.4234) = 0.906 s` at 45 degrees and 0.746 s at 0 degrees. Assertion at defaults: `2.2 / sqrt(2) = 1.556 >= 1 / (1 - cos(pi x 0.40 x 1.0)) = 1.447` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.

The same follower carries the lie hand-off: a new lie on a ref in `RETURN` starts from its own formula and the ACTIVE slew (D.3) closes the gap from the in-flight value at `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`. **Binary frames** (a static-pair SPRITE_SWAP, PF-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a removal at or after the cut cuts the frame back at removal and the gleam decays on `nu(t)` through D.5's `g(nu)` on the `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` schedule, `(nu_end - LEAK_EPS_DEG) / GLIDE_RETURN_RATE = 19.75 / 3 = 6.6 s`; a removal inside the lead (`lie_tau < SWAP_LEAD_S`) never shows the false frame, and the gleam decays from the in-flight `nu_end` (vector: the vector lie `H(1, 0x1234, 7, 0)`, first breath period 5828 ms, removal at `lie_tau` 1.0 s, breath phase 0.172 so `breath01` 0.263, `nu_end` = `20 x smoothstep(1/3)` = 5.19 deg, the envelope `a_env` = `amp_snd_end` 550 and the gleam `amp_end` = `400 + (550 - 400) x 0.263` = 439 at stage 1; `nu` reaches `LEAK_EPS_DEG` at `(5.19 - 0.25) / 3` = 1.65 s, the gleam `amp` reaches 0 at `439 / 266.7` = 1.65 s, the sound `amp_snd` at `550 / 266.7` = 2.06 s, CLEAR at `WANDER_BLEND_S` 3.0 s). **Continuous frames** (the rotor, D.17) wind their cadence down at a constant rate and snap at the minimum cadence.
856	
857	**Example:** a 60-deg discrepancy at removal: 30 s at 2.0 deg/s, **20 s at 3.0**, 10 s at 6.0, and 24.0 s under reduced motion (`rm_ret` 0.83 gives 2.5 deg/s; it was 33.3 s at 1.8 deg/s) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A live 60-deg lie at 2.0 deg/s took 30 s to build, which is why the lower limit is `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`: below it a debunked needle would outlast a live lie, and a DEBUNKED would be a punishment. Flash coupling *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the ACTIVE-form coupling (0.0332 at the stage-3 floor) is withdrawn, so `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` and `LEAK_D_FULL_DEG` are no longer coupled by a flash ceiling (the `R_AMP` clamp bounds every fall; at rate 8 and `LEAK_D_FULL_DEG` 10 the unclamped slope would be 0.239 per second (1000 x 8 / 9.75 = 820 pm/s), and the clamp holds it at 0.0776). The amplitude-floor coupling: `0.291 x 400 / 1.5 / 1000 = 0.0776 < 0.10` (stage 0 to 1, the worst case; stage 3 is 0.0485). Binary frame: a cracked-housing frame cuts back at removal; the gleam, at 1000, decays to 0 over 6.6 s.

859	### D.7 Stage ramp envelope
860	
861	The stage ramp formula is defined as:
862	
863	`target_e = gate_e * GAIN_e[stage] / 1000`, with `gate_e = 1` for FLOOR and OUTLINE, `gate_RIM = 1` while Sanity's `reach_lie_active(P)` is true for the viewer (stage >= 2 and a listed entry with `away` false, `reach_tier` 2 and stepped PENDING to ACTIVE: an ACTIVE lie on a state glyph or lamp-housing glow sprite in the seat's current compartment; a machine-frame lie and any away lie do not drive it; PF-23; the only Filter read of `away`, PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* and 0 otherwise in LIE_BOUND mode (the shipped default; `gate_RIM = 1` in the opt-in AMBIENT mode), and `gate_BLEED = 1` only when `AMBIENT_FRINGES_ENABLED` is on (0 at the shipped default) (PF-23, PF-24, OQ-PF-1, OQ-PF-2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
864	
865	`r_e(t + dt) = r_e(t) + clamp(target_e - r_e(t), -rate_s * dt, +rate_s * dt)` with `rate_s = abs(target_e - r_e(t_s)) / STAGE_RAMP_S` latched at each target change `t_s`, on `present_time`, `hard_start: r_e := target_e`
866	
867	`effective_amplitude_e = r_e * amplitude_e`
868	
869	Build assertion: `STAGE_RAMP_S >= max(ramp_min(D.11), BREATH_MAX_MS / 1000 + RAMP_BREATH_MARGIN_S)`
870	
871	**Variables:**
872	
873	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
874	|---|---|---|---|---|
875	| `e` | enum | RIM, BLEED, FLOOR (and OUTLINE with `TELL_RAMP_S`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | PF-22, PF-28, D.5 | the stage-bound effect |
876	| `GAIN_e[stage]` | int pm | RIM `[0, 0, 600, 1000]`, BLEED `[0, 0, 0, 1000]` (`RIM_STAGE_GAIN_PM[2]`, `[3]`, `BLEED_STAGE_GAIN_PM[3]`, `[PLACEHOLDER]`), FLOOR `[0, 0, 500, 1000]` (`FLOOR_STAGE_GAIN_PM`, derived in D.5 as `(AMP_FLOOR_PM - floor(stage)) / (AMP_FLOOR_PM - AMP_FLOOR_S3_PM)`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | Filter | the envelope target per stage; `stage` is `sanity_view.stage`, which steps instantly at `STAGE_ENTER` 70000 / 55000 / 25000 with `STAGE_HYST` 2000 and `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` 25 (cited from Sanity's registry entry; the stage-2 entry was 45000 before X11/D64 raised it to 55000, and the Filter reads whatever Sanity registers) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* |
877	| `r_e` | float | [0, 1] | presentation-local | the envelope |
878	| `STAGE_RAMP_S` | float s | 8 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 6.5 to 20; registered | Filter | seconds for every envelope transition (a stage step or a reversal, whatever its size) |
879	| `TELL_RAMP_S` | float s | 8 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 6.5 to 15 | Filter | the same form for the class-(c) outline (VS-B) |
880	| `BREATH_MAX_MS` | int ms | 6000 (named here, value from ART 5.5 / HR-7) | art bible | the breath period upper bound |
881	| `RAMP_BREATH_MARGIN_S` | float s | 0.5 `[PLACEHOLDER]` | Filter | margin so the onset cannot read as one more breath |
882	| `dt` | float s | frame delta on `present_time`; 0 while PAUSED | PIPE PR-9 | the envelope's frame step |
883	| `t_s` | float s | >= 0 | `present_time` | the frame on which `target_e` last changed (a stage step or a reversal) |
884	| `rate_s` | float per s | 0 to `1 / STAGE_RAMP_S` | latched at `t_s` | the slew rate of the current transition, so that every transition takes `STAGE_RAMP_S` |
885	
886	**Output Range:** `r_e` is in [0, 1], slope at most `1 / STAGE_RAMP_S` = 0.125 per second, monotone between reversals, with no overshoot. Every transition, a reversal included, takes exactly `STAGE_RAMP_S`: the rate is re-latched from the current value, so a reversal from 0.5 returns to 0 in 8 s at 0.0625 per second. Because every transition (not only a full 0-to-1 swing) lasts `STAGE_RAMP_S`, the build assertion protects every MVP transition, including the 0.6 stage-2 step and the 0.6-to-1.0 stage-3 step. **Floor:** `STAGE_RAMP_S` and `TELL_RAMP_S` are held at or above `max(3.91 s (D.11 patch-level ramp_min), 6.0 + 0.5 s) = 6.5 s` by a build assertion; the breath rule governs, the flash model does not bind (D.11). The ramp's steepest slope (0.125 per second) is below the breath's steepest slope (`BREATH_DEPTH x pi / T_min = 0.47` per second), so a ramp reads as drift, not as a breath.
887	
888	**Example:** stage 1 to 2 at `t` 0, `STAGE_RAMP_S` 8: `r_RIM` rises at a latched 0.6 / 8 = 0.075 per second to its 0.6 target in **8.0 s**, longer than the 6 s breath upper bound. At 5 s (the earliest reversal, `STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` 25) the stage falls back to 1: `r_RIM` is 0.375, the rate re-latches to 0.375 / 8 = 0.047 per second, and it falls to 0 over the next 8.0 s, never restarting at 0. Stage 2 to 3: the target rises from 0.6 to 1.0 at 0.05 per second, in 8.0 s. `force_stage` 3: `r_RIM` is 1.0 on the first frame. The floor envelope runs the same form *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: stage 1 to 2 moves `r_FLOOR` from 0 to 0.5 in 8.0 s (`floor_eff` 400 to 325 at 9.4 pm/s) and stage 2 to 3 moves it 0.5 to 1.0 (325 to 250); `force_stage` 3 sets `floor_eff` 250 on the first frame; the RIM entry above assumes a reach lie is ACTIVE (LIE_BOUND), otherwise `target_RIM` is 0.

890	### D.8 Breath (per-cycle period, floor and harmonic dead zone)
891	
892	The breath formula is defined as:
893	
894	`T_n_ms = BREATH_MIN_MS + (h_cycle(n) mod 2001)`, then `T_n_ms = deadzone_push(T_n_ms, {2 * S_i, 3 * S_i : i in PERIODIC_SOURCES}, BREATH_DEADZONE_FRAC)`
895	
896	`phi_n(t + dt) = phi_n(t) + dt / (T_n_ms / 1000)`; at `phi >= 1`: `phi -= 1`, `n += 1`
897	
898	`amp_b = amp * (BREATH_FLOOR_PM + (1000 - BREATH_FLOOR_PM) * (0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2 * pi * phi))) / 1000`
899	
900	**Variables:**
901	
902	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
903	|---|---|---|---|---|
904	| `BREATH_MIN_MS`, `BREATH_MAX_MS` | int ms | 4000, 6000 (named here, values from ART 5.5 / HR-7) | art bible | the period band |
905	| `h_cycle(n)` | uint32 | 0 to 2^32 - 1 | D.14 (tag 1 plus the cycle index) | per-cycle draw of `H(viewer, ref_key, lie_key, epoch)`: a lie's gleam breath uses its own `(ref_key, lie_key)` with `epoch` 0; the rim, bleed and outline use the reserved effect ids and the envelope's `epoch` (D.14) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
906	| `S_i` | float ms | the alarm sweep `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` x 1000 / `TICK_RATE` (registered single alarm rhythm, Emitter State: 128 ticks = 2133 ms, range 120 to 180 = 2000 to 3000 ms; Audio's duty `ALARM_DUTY_MAX_PM` 250, leading edge is the contract, Audio CX-A20, F6; OQ-PF-13 closed); `tell_beat` period (Attention-owned) | owners | periodic sources to avoid locking to |
907	| `BREATH_DEADZONE_FRAC` | float | 0.06 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0 to 0.10 | Filter | half-width of the dead zone as a fraction of `k x S_i`; active for every registered `S_i` (the alarm sweep is) |
908	| `BREATH_LOCK_CEIL` | float | 0.30 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 0.2 to 0.5 (ratification OQ-PF-24) | Filter / systems-designer | peak normalised cross-correlation a breath may show against a periodic source (AC-PF-27) |
909	| `deadzone_push` | function | int ms in, int ms in [`BREATH_MIN_MS`, `BREATH_MAX_MS`] out | Filter (D.8) | redraw with the cycle index bumped up to 3 times, else clamp to the nearer zone boundary inside the band (deterministic) |
910	| `BREATH_FLOOR_PM` | int pm | 400 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 250 to 700 (PF-30) | Filter | the trough, never 0 (a fringe that blinks out is unleaked) |
911	| `amp` | int pm | 0 to 1000 | the fringe's stage envelope (D.7) or the outline envelope | the amplitude being modulated |
912	| `phi` | float | [0, 1) | `present_time` | cycle phase; the cosine minimum is at the wrap, so a period change never kinks |
913	
914	**Output Range:** `T_n` is in [4000, 6000] ms minus any dead zone; `amp_b` is in `[amp x BREATH_FLOOR_PM / 1000, amp]`. **The harmonic:** every legal period equals `2S` for some sweep period `S` in 2 to 3 s (and `3S` at the 6 s edge when `S` is 2 s), so a fixed period locks 2:1 against a fixed sweep; SNV-26 forbids locking. Per-cycle jitter makes an accidental alignment last about one cycle in expectation, and the dead zone closes the rest. With `S` 2.5 s the zone is `5000 x (1 +- 0.06)` = [4700, 5300] ms (30 % of the band); with `S` 2.0 s the zones are [3760, 4240] and [5640, 6360], leaving [4240, 5640]; at the registered `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (`S` 2133 ms) the zone around `2S` is [4011, 4523] ms and `3S` (6400 ms, zone [6016, 6784]) lies outside the band.
915	
916	**Example:** `H(1, 0x1234, 7, 0)` (D.14), cycle 0: `h_cycle(0) mod 2001` = 1828, so `T_0 = 5828 ms`; cycle 1: 1740 gives `T_1 = 5740 ms`; cycle 2: `T_2 = 5735 ms`. At `phi` 0.5 `amp_b = amp`; at `phi` 0 `amp_b = 0.4 amp`. Two simultaneous fringes use different `(subject, seat)` keys and therefore different sequences.
917	
918	**The lie gleam breath and the sound envelope** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the same per-cycle draw drives the static-pair gleam breath (PF-15 table): D.5's `breath01(phi)` swings the gleam between `floor_eff` and `AMP_MAX_PM` (depth 0.6 at stages 0 to 1, the same `d_b` as the fringe; 0.75 at stage 3, `d_g` of D.11, re-checked there) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, keyed on the lie's `(viewer, ref_key, lie_key, 0)` and dead-zoned like the fringe; the lie's own cycle 0 starts at its trough (`phi := 0` on the first ACTIVE frame and at `hard_start`, a presentation-local phase), so the onset step of D.5 is followed by a rise, never a fall, for at least half a period (2 s) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The sound envelope of PF-20 draws one period per lie from tag 11, `T_s = 4000 + (sub(H, 11) mod 2001)` ms, dead-zoned, trough `SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM`: 5473 ms for `H(1, 0x1234, 7, 0)`.
919	
920	### D.9 Lying-digit tick schedule
921	
922	The lying-digit tick formula is defined as:
923	
924	`T_tick = max(LIE_TICK_MS, N_r * 334)`
925	
926	`t_k = k * T_tick + j * T_tick / N_r` on `present_time`, `j` the readout's stagger index (ordered by hash tag 6); the stagger spacing `T_tick / N_r` is never below 334 ms, the single-readout floor
927	
928	`q_k = clamp(round(slew_value(t_k) / lsb), q_lo, q_hi)`, `q_lo = round(value_lo / lsb)`, `q_hi = round(value_hi / lsb)`; in TICK mode, if `q_k == q_{k-1}`, `q_k = q_{k-1} + sgn_k` (one `lsb`, sign from hash tag 6, flipped if it would leave `[q_lo, q_hi]`), so the digit changes every tick; in STALE mode `q_k` follows the **displayed** needle value by ticks while the lie is in ONSET and is **held from arrival** (when `delta_pm` reaches its aim), never the zone centre while the needle is still short of it, so the digit does not change while the ship changes. During RETURN the numeral keeps the TICK rule on the returning `slew_value` and switches to the honest grid at CLEAR (PF-18). A region gap governor defers any lying tick due less than 334 ms after the previous lying tick in the region; it never defers an honest swap, and the lying-to-honest switch lands on the next HUD grid boundary (PF-18) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
929	
930	**Variables:**
931	
932	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
933	|---|---|---|---|---|
934	| `LIE_TICK_MS` | int ms | 400 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 334 to 1000; registered | Filter | single-readout interval. The **floor is 334 ms**: 333 ms is 3.003 transitions per second against AC-SN-149 "no more than 3 per second" |
935	| `N_r` | int | 1 to `LIES_MAX` (4, cited, Sanity) | derived | lying readouts in the same ninth of the displayed picture, counting HUD-layer readouts |
936	| `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` | int | 3 (cited, Pipeline) | registry | transition ceiling |
937	| `lsb` | number | > 0 | calibration record (PF-45) | the readout's least-significant unit (one display unit) |
938	| `q_lo`, `q_hi` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int | `round(value_lo / lsb)`, `round(value_hi / lsb)` | calibration record (PF-45) | the numeral's valid range in `lsb` steps; every TICK and STALE value is clamped to it, and the TICK step flips sign rather than leave it |
939	| `mode` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: `params.readout_mode`)* | enum | TICK (`readout_mode` 1), STALE (`readout_mode` 2) | `params.readout_mode`, or the kind map for a NEEDLE entry's numeral (GLIDE gives TICK; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL give STALE; PF-18) | the two lying-readout modes; never a hash draw (hash tag 6 keeps its only uses, the stagger order and the TICK step sign) |
940	
941	**Output Range:** `T_tick` in {400, 668, 1002, 1336} ms for `N_r` 1 to 4 at the default, with stagger spacing 400, 334, 334 and 334 ms; because consecutive transitions in a region are at least 334 ms apart, no closed 1 s window holds more than 3 (the reasoning that set the 334 ms single-readout floor), and the mean rate `N_r / T_tick` is 2.50, 2.994, 2.994 and 2.994 per second. Without the scheduler four readouts at 400 ms would make 10 transitions per second, 3.3 times the ceiling. At `N_r` 4 the continuous cadence falls to 0.75 Hz: still never stopped, still distinguishable from an honest numeral (which changes on the HUD-owned `HONEST_TICK_MS` hold grid), but weaker (risk in Open Questions). Reduced motion never lowers `LIE_TICK_MS` (it may be raised to 600). When `N_r` changes mid-run (a lie starts or ends) `T_tick` is re-evaluated at the next tick and the gap governor still guarantees 334 ms between lying ticks across the change, and the lying-to-honest switch at CLEAR lands on the next HUD grid boundary, where the HUD arbiter (not the governor) admits or skips it (AC-PF-75b, AC-PF-75c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
942	
943	**Example:** three lying readouts in one region: `T_tick = max(400, 3 x 334) = 1002 ms` each, phases 0, 334 and 668 ms, so transitions fall every 334 ms: a closed 1 s window from 0 holds 0, 334 and 668 ms (the next is at 1002 ms), never four.
944	
945	**Flash counting unit and the honest numerals (USER RULING X9/D91, OQ-PF-12)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): a flash event is one opposing pair of luminance transitions, so the counting unit is `flash_events = ceil(n_transitions / 2)` over a rolling second (the registry's `flash_count`), and `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` is weighted per area with the creative-director exemptions (sub-threshold digit swaps and prompt show-starts exempt; the strict ceiling kept for the Alarm Red mark and under reduce-flashing, which defaults ON at first launch, X10). Filter side: D.9 does **not** use the headroom the unit allows. The scheduler keeps the strict transition form (`N_r / T_tick <= 3` transitions per second, 334 ms gap) because Sanity's AC-SN-149 ("no more than 3 changes per second") is a transition cap, a separate rule from the flash unit, and because the strict ceiling is the one that binds under the default reduce-flashing setting. Honest numerals on the ratified `HONEST_TICK_MS` 500 ms grid are sub-threshold digit swaps and, in WEIGHTED mode, are exempt, so they take no slot in `N_r` (in STRICT, the reduce-flashing default, they are counted and the HUD arbiter skips an honest swap the window cannot hold: PF-18, AC-PF-75c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; even counted, the worst case is 2 transitions per second per numeral, and a region holding the Filter's 3 lying transitions plus one honest numeral's 2 is `ceil((3 + 2) / 2) = 3 <= FLASH_MAX_PER_S`.
946	
947	### D.10 Fringe width at ladder step k
948	
949	The fringe width formula is defined as:
950	
951	`W_screen(n, k) = n * k` screen px for a mark of `n` art px
952	
953	`n = RIM_FRINGE_PX` (rim band), `n = 2` (crewmate outline, fixed by ART 5.5, not a knob), `n = GLEAM_EDGE_PX` (gleam), `k in [1, k_auto + 2]`, `k_auto = floor(min(W / 640, H / 360))`
954	
955	**Variables:**
956	
957	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
958	|---|---|---|---|---|
959	| `n` | int art px | 1 to 3 | `RIM_FRINGE_PX` 2 `[PLACEHOLDER]` (1 to 3), outline 2 (fixed), `GLEAM_EDGE_PX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (1 to 2; 2 at `k` 1, else 1, per Instruments' `gleam_edge_px`) | mark width in the 640x360 grid |
960	| `k` | int | 1 to 8 | PIPE PR-1, C6 (cited) | integer zoom step |
961	| `W`, `H` | int px | display size | OS | the window's pixel size |
962	
963	**Output Range:** `W_screen` is always an exact integer multiple of `k` (no sub-art-pixel softness), from 1 (rim 1 at `k` 1; the gleam is never below 2) to 24 (rim 3 at `k` 8). Under render pass B the leak material takes `k` as a uniform and does no arithmetic on it. A zoom change is a cut (PIPE C6): widths are re-derived on the first frame of the new rung and never interpolated.
964	
965	**Example:**
966	
967	| Display | `k_auto` | Ladder | Rim (n = 2) | Outline (n = 2) | Gleam (n = 2 at `k` 1, else 1) |
968	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
969	| 1280x720 (Steam Deck class) | 2 | 1 to 4 | 2, 4, 6, 8 px | same | 2, 2, 3, 4 px |
970	| 1920x1080 | 3 | 1 to 5 | 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 px | same | 2, 2, 3, 4, 5 px |
971	| 3840x2160 | 6 | 1 to 8 | 2, 4, ... 16 px | same | 2, 2, 3, ... 8 px |
972	
973	At `k` 1 on 2160p the field is 3840x2160 art px (36 times the default 640x360 area) and a 2-px band is 2 screen px: legibility is OQ-PF-4 (PIPE OQ 4).

975	### D.11 Flash model
976	
977	The flash model formula is defined as:
978	
979	(a) region bound: `dY_region(1 s) = sum_e (a_e / A_region_min(k)) * Y_v * dAmp_e(1 s)`, required `dY_region <= FILTER_FLASH_MARGIN` **at every rung `k` of the ladder, evaluated at the smallest field** (`A_region_min(k) = W x H / (9 k^2)` in art px^2, the top rung `k_auto + 2` being the worst) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; if the margin is under 1 at a rung, the per-region cap on **breathing elements only**, `N_G_REGION(k) = max(0, floor((FILTER_FLASH_MARGIN x A_region_min(k) / Y_v - a_rim x dAmp - a_other x dAmp_other) / (a_gleam x dAmp)))` (`a_other x dAmp_other` = 20 x 100 x 0.06 = 120 for the non-breathing gleams), limits the simultaneous breathing gleams in one ninth of the picture, and the excess lies (newest first) take the honest path with `filter_draws_dropped`, never a lie without its gleam; it is a boundary guard that binds only at the smallest field
980	
981	(b) patch-level pair bound: `Y_v * (ramp_slope * W + b_pair) < FLASH_LUM_DELTA`, `b_pair = d_b * (1 - cos(pi * W / T_min)) / 2`, `d_b = 1 - BREATH_FLOOR_PM / 1000`, `ramp_min = 1 / (FLASH_LUM_DELTA / Y_v - b_pair)`
982	
983	(c) count bound: `N_b <= N_B_MAX = floor(FLASH_MAX_PER_S * T_min_s)`
984	
985	**Variables:**
986

192	### Core Rules
193	
194	*Conventions.* Rules are named `PF-n`; each states a **Rule**, a **Why** and **Edge notes**. Formulas are `D.n` (Formulas section, written in part 2 of this document; the rules below fix *what* each formula must compute and its binding constants, and name it). Every pixel measure is in **art px of the 640x360 base picture**; on screen it is `k` times larger at integer zoom `k` in `[1, k_auto + 2]` (`k_auto = floor(min(W/640, H/360))`, PIPE PR-1, C6). Registry constants are cited by **name and registry value**; a number marked `[PLACEHOLDER]` is invented here, carries a range and a proposed registered name, and is final nowhere (reflexion: a placeholder never becomes a fact). Upstream facts are cited by rule id first (`SN-15 L-L`, `HE-40`). Anything about Accessibility Settings or Co-op Session is **(provisional — undesigned)**; HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments & Inspect View, Debug Overlay (True Values) and Adaptive Audio & Tells have since been designed and their answers are recorded in Interactions I-B and OQ-PF-29 (2026-10-27 consistency pass). For the undesigned neighbours: this GDD places a requirement on the neighbour and describes what the Filter *returns*, never the neighbour's internals. There is no `scripting.md` or `core.md` in `docs/engine-reference/godot/`: GDScript integer-overflow, `Dictionary` ordering, `RefCounted` lifetime and per-call cost are **not sourceable** and are marked `[UNV]` wherever a rule depends on them; the reference also carries nothing on `canvas_item` shader instance parameters, container materials or viewport masking, so every shading-language mechanism is a `[UNV]` spike item, never the basis of a rule.
195	
196	#### A. Architecture, channels and the tag contract
197	
198	**PF-1. Channel architecture: consume, do not own.**
199	*Rule.* The Filter registers no kernel block, no step hook and no mutator (KERN CR-3, CR-8, CR-9). The `PERCEPTION_OUT` block of the routed thread is `sanity.perception`, which the Filter consumes. The Filter's **perceived channel** (the `Perceived` records, the lie trajectories, the per-viewer decoy list, the rim and outline state) is a presentation-side surface that inherits every `PERCEPTION_OUT` rule: no simulation system reads it (kernel H5), it is never persisted, it is never part of `state_hash` (KERN D.12). KERN C.3 row 11 grants the Filter "Subscriptions only ... Neither gets submit or mutators"; it subscribes as `PRESENTATION`.
200	*Why.* A `PRESENTATION` subscriber cannot write a block (H3, H4), and the kernel defines the class as Sanity's output. Stating the reading on page one keeps a reviewer from reading the thread literally.
201	*Edge notes.* Lighting's row says "a per-client `PERCEPTION_OUT` decoy list"; under this rule that list is a Filter-published presentation list (refresh row 20). -> ADR candidate: Filter channel architecture and the "no block" ruling. (orchestrator ruling R1.)
202	
203	**PF-2. Write set.**
204	*Rule.* The Filter writes `CanvasItem` members, `Material` and shader parameters (including per-instance parameters), particle members and audio *requests*. It writes **no member of any real light** (LO-25 (ii): "the Filter writes no `Light2D` member"), no `Camera2D`, `Viewport`, `SubViewport` or `SubViewportContainer` property (PIPE C1, C9; the container's `material` slot is assigned and nulled by the pipeline root, PF-25), no simulation state and no block. A grep-able lint enforces every clause (AC-PF-8).
205	*Why.* The true reveal radius is an anchor (EM-29); a Filter-written light member would be a path to move it. The six upstream clauses that still say "CanvasItem/Material/Light2D" are stale tokens (Cross-References, refresh table), not authority.
206	*Edge notes.* `Light2D` appears in this GDD only in the negative or inside a quotation of a stale clause. (orchestrator ruling R2.)
207	
208	**PF-3. Read set and handles.**
209	*Rule.* The Filter reads: `sanity.perception` (local owner only), the SIM view `sanity_view(player_id) -> {stage, tell_on, harm_eligible}`, Graph `true_value(kind, id)` and Suit `true_value(key, player_id)` (it is the **only non-diagnostic caller** of either, LS-19, LS-22, SE-29), the kernel read views of true positions (`horror.view`, Body and Controller views, for placement only), the tick count, `tick_alpha` and the Pipeline's `present_time`. It **holds no handle on `sanity.state` or `sanity.ledger`** ("no Sanity symbol reads a Filter value, and the Filter holds no handle on `sanity.state` or `sanity.ledger`", SN-23). It imports no simulation module, never registers or moves an Interaction subject (IA-13) and never submits a command.
210	*Why.* One wrap point, one place the Debug Overlay hooks, and a one-way edge: Sanity writes, the Filter draws, nothing flows back.
211	*Edge notes.* The HUD never calls Suit's `true_value`; it calls `perceived(SUIT_KEY(k), viewer)`, which wraps it (refresh row 11, X10). The Filter never reads `served_pm`, `lit` or any Attention value to *draw* anything.
212	
213	**PF-4. Default TRUTH, four grades.**
214	*Rule.* Every presentation node under the world layer is TRUTH unless it carries a `PerceptionTag` of another grade. Grades: **TRUTH_PX** (bit-identical pixels with the Filter on or off); **TRUTH_ST** (state, shape, position and existence never moved, added or removed; a colour-only edge tint inside ART 4.4 is allowed); **LEAK** (truth by construction: the leak elements themselves, which "cannot be faked or suppressed by any other lie"); **CORRUPTIBLE** (a named module-body surface carrying a `lie_surface_id` present in `lie_targets.json`). An untagged node is TRUTH (counted in `tag_defaults_applied`, never an error).
215	*Why.* A forgotten node that lies about the consequence channel is the one unrecoverable P1 failure; a forgotten instrument that never lies is a content bug caught by a coverage lint (AC-PF-6). The consequence of default-TRUTH is that the failure mode of omission is "the lie vanishes", never "the truth breaks".
216	*Edge notes.* Layout's request that walls be truth is granted in full at grade TRUTH_ST (colour-only tint allowed, geometry never touched); Layout's narrower fallback (ordinary interior door leaves at the Filter's discretion) is recorded, not adopted (OQ-PF-14). (orchestrator ruling R11.)

240	| 17b | The pipe's fitting silhouette **edge** (the colour-blind shape backup keeps its shape; only a colour-only edge tint is allowed, stage 3, cuttable) | TRUTH_ST (the same grade, and for the same reason, as Layout's walls, X9) | SN-15 table; ART 4.4; PF-24 |
241	| 18 | Gouged WORN footprints of a real horror, while that entity is registered | TRUTH | SN-15 L-C |
242	| 19 | **The leaks**: gleam, own-cone rim fringe, crewmate-outline fringe, stage-3 hue bleed | LEAK | SN visual table; ART Corollary |
243	| 20 | **Corruptible set, MVP-live**: gauge needle (dial arc), digital readout, state glyph, inspect card (the same instrument as its wall gauge, from stage 1), lamp-housing glow **sprite** (appearance frame only), whole machine sprite state frames (stage 3; both honest frames required) | CORRUPTIBLE, each with a tri-modal leak | SN-16; SNV-7 to SNV-9; LS:864 |
244	| 21 | **Corruptible set, VS-A and VS-B** (designed, tested with stubs) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)*: WORN descriptors (demoted from MVP-live: no `PerceptionRef` exists, PF-9; Sanity's published `surface` set has no WORN value, so it stays VS-A with no ref, OQ-PF-38 item 4 closed 2026-10-28 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*), `suit.*` readings behind `READING_LIE_STAGE`, scanner at stage 3, decoy overlays, phantom rigs, HIDE of a real body, lure dressing, the class-(c) horror rig on a crewmate (beam and voice stay TRUTH) | CORRUPTIBLE | SN-19 to SN-22 |
245	
246	*Why.* P1: "Subtle is allowed; absent is not" applies to the leaks; the closed lists apply to everything else. Rows 17a and 17b follow Sanity's art-director classification over LO-14's "pipe flow" (X5): a running pipe is a world-state witness and its shape is the colour-blind backup. Radiator glow sprite, lamp-housing glow sprite and breaker-panel lamp stay corruptible (LS:213).
247	*Edge notes.* The lamp-housing lie swaps an **appearance frame** only: the real lamp light, pool and `lux` never change (AC-SN-122). **Must repeat (MSA-35, MSA F1):** Assembly reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block and writes no perception state; the Filter never wraps seam geometry, bead, cap plate, socket state or `CUT_BLOCKED`, never fakes or suppresses an install prompt, and, until Graph ASK G8 and F&T ASK FT1 are answered, never wraps the sprites of the seam's own PIPE and DUCT valves and CABLE breaker (MSA-23 fallback). MSA-35's allowance of a phantom seam or a false "welded" state in the Filter's corruptible layer is not used: no seam surface is in `lie_targets.json`, and rows 11 and 12 bar one while F1 stands. (orchestrator ruling R11, R13.)
248	
249	**PF-6. Tag contract and lints.**
250	*Rule.* A `PerceptionTag` resource on each presentation scene root carries `{class: TRUTH_PX | TRUTH_ST | LEAK | CORRUPTIBLE, lie_surface_id}`; a CORRUPTIBLE dial or readout surface also carries the calibration record of PF-45 (supplied by the owning scene). The decision logic lives in a headless-testable resolver. Build-failing lints: (i) CORRUPTIBLE requires a `lie_surface_id` present in `lie_targets.json`; (ii) **no TRUTH_PX node has any Filter leak parameter at a non-rest value in any frame**, and on a TRUTH_ST node only `edge_bleed_pm` may be non-rest, and only where the sheet's edge channel is set and its emission channel is clear (PF-24); the lint is at parameter level because the lit leak family lives as a default-off block inside the shared HullSurface and Emissive materials (PF-43), so a node may carry the shared material and still be bit-identical; (iii) the wrapped-sprite registry holds no seam-lane valve or breaker id (row 12); (iv) the Filter source imports no simulation module and writes no block, `Camera2D`, `Viewport`, `SubViewport`, `SubViewportContainer` or real-light member; (v) no Filter code path calls `register_subject`, moves a subject or submits a command (IA-13, AC-IA-85); (vi) coverage: every module kind in `lie_targets.json` has at least one tagged CORRUPTIBLE surface in the MVP content (a VS-A WORN row is not counted and not required, PF-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (vii) no Filter code path calls `set_shader_parameter` on a material referenced by more than one node *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
251	*Why.* Behaviour plus lint, not a class layout. -> ADR candidate: tag mechanism and default-deny.
252	*Edge notes.* Lint (ii) is reworded from the rulings' "no Filter material on any TRUTH-tagged node" to parameter level because the stage-3 pipe-edge bleed puts a Filter-written parameter on a shared pipe material whose silhouette edge is graded TRUTH_ST (row 17b) while its emission, chevrons, pattern and diameter stay TRUTH_PX (row 17a); the parameter-level reading keeps the lint testable (CONFLICT C-2 below). (orchestrator ruling R12.)
253	
254	**PF-7. The query.**
255	*Rule.* `perceived(ref: PerceptionRef, viewer: PlayerId) -> Perceived` is the only way a corruptible node obtains a displayed value. It is a pull, called from the render callback, deterministic in `(the sanity.perception entry for ref, the true value, the lie's sim-time age, present_time-driven phases, viewer)` modulo the presentation-local state of PF-11. **Cheap honest path:** with no entry for `ref`, `displayed` equals the true value, `leak_amplitude_pm` is 0, `motion_mode` is HONEST, nothing is allocated. Instruments and the HUD never call `true_value`; the Debug Overlay (DIAGNOSTIC) calls both `true_value` and `perceived` for the same ref (PF-41). Results are memoised per `(ref, viewer, frame)`; an honest ref is further memoised per sanity run and invalidated by the notification that dirtied it (so an honest gauge never lags its own settle).
256	*Why.* One call keeps one wrap point and one debug hook. It mirrors Suit's `true_value(key, player_id)`. The wall gauge, its inspect card and the Debug Overlay's "perceived" column cost one evaluation, and card-gauge parity (HR-14, IA-38) holds by construction.
257	*Edge notes.* Instruments apply their honest settle and tremor **only when `motion_mode` is HONEST**. (orchestrator ruling R8.)
