content.content:
329	
330	| Surface class | Lie kinds | Hue-independent motion mode (`motion_mode`) | Notes |
331	|---|---|---|---|
332	| Dial gauge needle (GRAPH_NODE, GRAPH_COMPARTMENT, SUIT_KEY dial) | GLIDE, FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL | needle drift plus the never-rest wander (record mode GLIDE, or STALE for FALSE_*); the card numeral adds TICK or STALE | the wander runs in every needle lie, including one whose truth sits at a dial stop (D.3 live clamp, E-PF-10); a needle shorter than `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` is not lied on unless the ref has a visible digit mechanism (E-PF-11) |
333	| Linear sight-glass | same | meniscus drift plus the wander (PF-45 linear branch) | below `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` not lied on |
334	| Numeral-only readout (digit mechanism, no needle) | GLIDE; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL | TICK for GLIDE; for FALSE_* STALE **plus the gleam breath** (a held digit alone is not motion, so the record carries BREATH's gleam modulation) | D.9 |
335	| State glyph, lamp-housing glow, machine state (static pair) | SPRITE_SWAP; FALSE_OK, FALSE_FAIL on a housing appearance frame | BREATH: the gleam breathes between `floor_eff` (D.5) and `AMP_MAX_PM` over 4 to 6 s (D.8; HR-7 already treats the breath as a fringe's hue-independent channel) | the false frame itself is static; E-PF-12 |
336	| Machine sprite, continuous frame (rotor on a stopped machine) | SPRITE_SWAP | the rotor cadence drift (record mode GLIDE, D.17) | |
337	
338	*Why.* "Subtle is allowed; absent is not" (ART:73). The earlier draft let the hash choose *which* of the three modes to drop, so a stage-2 or stage-3 lie could have been drawn as glide plus sound with no violet anywhere, breaking the pillar's sane-palette clause (creative-director concern, CD-GDD-ALIGN); the palette mode is now mandatory exactly as the motion mode already was. The stage-2 rim fringe and the stage-3 hue bleed are not relied on to cover a gap, because both are conditional and cuttable. A leak that is a pure function of discrepancy is 0 on the first frame, which would break SN-15 L-L ("the first lie carries all three") and SNV-13 ("full leak from frame one"); the floor closes that onset hole. The `AMP_FLOOR_PM` visibility floor is a sibling of `DECOY_LEAK_ALPHA_PM` 300 and `BREATH_FLOOR_PM` 400 at stages 0 to 2 (the gleam floor is 400 and 325); at stage 3 the user-ruled floor of 250 (D74) deliberately sits below the decoy's 300 (a VS-A overlay, absent at MVP), and the alignment is routed to Lighting and the art-director. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
339	*Edge notes.* A malformed entry with empty `leak_modes`, or with a non-empty `leak_modes` that lacks the GLEAM bit, is a debug-build assertion; release draws GLEAM and GLIDE for the empty entry, **adds GLEAM** to the other, and counts `leak_repaired`, so a palette-silent lie is never drawn (E-PF-49). If audio is muted or unavailable the lie keeps two modes; the player's mute is not a Filter event.
340	
341	**PF-16. The gleam.**
342	*Rule.* Violet `#B07BE6` (never the core `#8A3FD1`), at an **edge only** (glass edge, needle leading edge, housing edge, sprite contour), never a fill or a plane, `GLEAM_EDGE_PX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (range 1 to 2), set per rung by Instruments' `gleam_edge_px`: 2 art px at k = 1 and 1 art px at k >= 2, so the gleam is at least 2 screen px at every rung (`GLEAM_EDGE_SCREEN_MIN` 2, OQ-IW-4 accepted inside this range). It is drawn on the corruptible element itself, **lit with its host** (it appears only where the instrument is visible; no lit-gate query is needed and none is made, IA-13), and its amplitude is the PF-15 amplitude (breathing on the static-pair classes, D.5). Its transport is the ladder of PF-42 (instance parameters, then a MultiMesh overlay, else the surface is not lied on); a MultiMesh path must keep the gleam lit with its host and sample the host's `_msk` edge slice, which is spike S-1c *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Its peak channel is capped at `LEAK_MAX_CH`, defined **by relation** as `LEAK_MAX_CH := DECOY_MAX_CH` (0.85, itself at most 0.9 x `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD`; `DECOY_MAX_CH` is registered and owned by Lighting; `LEAK_MAX_CH` is a name introduced here for the registry stage, not a knob and not a second value), so a leak never blooms (glow is processed before tonemapping since 4.6) and never reads as a light.
343	*Why.* A gleam on an unlit instrument would be a location oracle and would put a phantom in the dark (SN:1267). The cost of the lit choice is that the on-screen colour shifts under the Tungsten beam (the blue channel is attenuated about a third), which the art-director must accept (OQ-PF-6); the hue-removed test (AC-SN-154) is unaffected.
344	*Edge notes.* On a HUD-layer reading (VS-A) the HUD draws the gleam on its own glass, in HUD px, from `leak_amplitude_pm` and `leak_modes`; the inspect card's glass is drawn by its owning node the same way (Instruments IW-16, with the HUD's gleam helper). The Filter supplies parameters and owns no HUD node (C-3 and OQ-PF-11 closed from the HUD side, OQ-HS-16). `LEAK_MAX_CH` is a **linear** channel value, compared in the same space as `GLOW_HDR_THRESHOLD` (pre-tonemap), and applies on every surface the Filter parameterises, world layer and HUD-layer glass alike; if HDR output is enabled on the root viewport the cap is re-tested (OQ-HS-13; `[UNV]` until the Lighting spike confirms the colour space of `DECOY_MAX_CH`).
345	
346	**PF-17. Motion signatures and the never-rest rule.**
347	*Rule.* Exactly three motion signatures exist and only one belongs to a lie: **settle** (damped spring, ease-out 250 to 400 ms, overshoot at most 5 %, then still), **tremor** (+-1 art px (+-2 art px at k = 1, so it stays at least 2 screen px; Instruments' `tremor_offset`), irregular, 6 to 10 Hz, around a *true* value) and **glide** (the lie). A lie never borrows settle or tremor; an honest gauge never glides; the returned `motion_mode` is the only switch. The leak's own HR-7 breath (D.8) is a modulation of the gleam and not a fourth gait: it is the motion mode of the static-pair classes (PF-15 table) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Never-rest:** the 0.5 to 2 deg/s band of ART 7.3 bounds the *drift* component only; a separate **wander**, one sinusoid per lie, of `WANDER_AMP_PX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (2.2 art px at the needle tip, along the needle's tangent; range 2.1 to 2.6 at `WANDER_F_MIN` 0.40, the lower bound being derived in D.4 for the worst needle angle; the art-director's floor of 1 px is met with margin) at a hashed frequency in `WANDER_F_MIN` to `WANDER_F_MAX` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (0.40 to 0.45 Hz; below the 0.5 Hz cap, and disjoint from the 6 to 10 Hz tremor) carries "never rests" for a held lie. (orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's two-sine sum is not adopted, because its beat envelope falls to 0.2 of the peak and the rounded tip would then rest; D.4.) A held lie's tip changes its quantised pixel position at least every `NEVER_REST_MAX_S`, a **cited ceiling of 1.0 s** (ART 7.3 and SNV-25: "the needle is always a pixel from where it was a second ago"; not tunable above 1.0 s), proven in D.4 **on two axes** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the tip moves along the needle's tangent, so at tangent angle `phi` the rounded tip position is a pair of rounded axis positions, and the worst-case dwell on one pixel is `acos(1 - 1/(A m)) / (pi f)` with `m = max(abs(cos phi), abs(sin phi))`, at least `1/sqrt(2)`: the worst needle angle is 45 degrees, where each axis sees only `A / sqrt(2)`. The single-axis figure of the earlier draft (0.952 s at 2.0 px and 0.35 Hz) hid a **1.16 s rest at 45 degrees**, over the art bible's 1.0 s ceiling, which no amplitude inside the old range could fix; so `WANDER_F_MIN` is **0.40 Hz** (range 0.40 to 0.45) and `WANDER_AMP_PX` 2.2 (worst case 0.96 s at 45 degrees, 0.79 s at 0 and 90 degrees). Lie-capable in-world gauges ship a needle of at least 16 art px (recommended 24); a needle shorter than `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 16; range 14.3 to 32; eligibility floor 14.3 = 28.6 / `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`; owner In-World Instruments, provisional) is ineligible for a needle glide **and the surface is not lied on at all** (E-PF-11: a gleam with a sound has no hue-independent motion mode), unless the same ref has a visible digit mechanism whose TICK, or STALE with the gleam breath, is then its motion mode *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
348	*Why.* At 0.5 to 2 deg/s a 12 to 32 px needle's tip moves 0.1 to 1.1 art px per second, one pixel step every 1 to 10 s, so "always a pixel from where it was a second ago" (ART 7.3, HR-8, SNV-25) is unattainable by rotation alone. The wander also exceeds 2 deg/s instantaneous angular speed on a short needle (14.9 deg/s at 24 px, 2.2 px and 0.45 Hz), which is why the band is read as drift only. (CONFLICT C-1: the art bible's glide band and its own never-rest sentence; the bible refresh is owed by the art-director, Cross-References.)
349	*Edge notes.* The per-lie drift rate is raised to `rate_floor = max(0.5, 28.6 / needle_len_px)` so tip speed is at least 0.5 art px per second where the band allows (at 24 px, 1.2 deg/s). **HUD dials (VS-A; OQ-HS-12).** The glide-eligibility rule is the same for a HUD-layer dial: `needle_len_px` and `NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` are measured in the pixel grid the dial is drawn in (HUD px), so the rate floor keeps the tip at least 0.5 px of that grid per second; a HUD dial whose needle is shorter is not lied on (E-PF-11), unless it has a visible digit mechanism whose TICK or STALE is its motion mode *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The charge cell's motion mode is not ruled here (OQ-PF-33). Reduced motion does not scale the wander amplitude or frequency (PF-39), so the 1.0 s ceiling is untouched by `RM_GLIDE_SCALE`. The wander is added outside the slew of PF-13, which would otherwise clip its instantaneous speed. **Onset rule and maximum onset rest** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at a lie's first ACTIVE frame the gauge is usually still (a settled honest needle), so the wander fades in *linearly over `WANDER_ONSET_S`* (`[PLACEHOLDER]` 1.0 s; range 0.5 to 3.0; linear, because the smoothstep of the earlier draft left the tip on one pixel for over 2 s) from a zero offset on frame one (no first-frame jump, D.1), and any honest tremor already running is blended out, not stopped, by `tremor_weight_pm` (PF-8) over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` := `WANDER_ONSET_S`. The maximum onset rest is `ONSET_REST_MAX_S` := `WANDER_ONSET_S + NEVER_REST_MAX_S` = 2.0 s (analytic bound: the fade-in, then the held-state ceiling); the worst case measured over needle angle, phase and fractional pixel is 1.15 s at 0.40 Hz (D.4, AC-PF-46). The gleam and the sound are on from frame one, so an onset rest is never a moment without a leak.
350	
351	**PF-18. Lying readouts: tick, stale-hold and card parity.**
352	*Rule.* A lying digital readout either **ticks continuously** (the digit tracks the glide) or **holds stale** (the digit holds the false target while the ship changes), as Sanity publishes *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: `params.readout_mode`)*: for a READOUT entry the numeral mode is `params.readout_mode` (1 TICK, 2 STALE); for the card numeral of a NEEDLE entry (params `{}`) it is derived from the kind by a pure map (GLIDE gives TICK; FALSE_OK and FALSE_FAIL give STALE). No hash chooses the mode. Sanity defines `readout_mode` by the same map; on a disagreement the published value wins and a debug-build assertion fires. The readout is the card numeral (the `displayed_value` of the needle ref's `Perceived`); TICK and STALE govern that numeral only, while the needle draws `displayed_pm` with the never-rest wander in every non-HONEST mode (PF-8; Instruments C2, OQ-IW-19). Honest numerals update on the shared hold grid `HONEST_TICK_MS` (500 ms, HUD-owned; at most one step per grid boundary, then-current value, never queued) and never tween (registry `honest_numeral`; the grid amends art bible 7.3's "one step per real change", ratified 2026-10-27, user ruling X9/D91 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*). The tick interval is `LIE_TICK_MS` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (registered; default 400 ms; range 334 to 1000): the floor is **334 ms**, because a 333 ms interval is 3.003 transitions per second against AC-SN-149 "no more than 3 per second" and the registered intent of `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3. Lying readouts that share a region (a ninth of the displayed picture, counting HUD-layer readouts) share one scheduler: `T_tick = max(LIE_TICK_MS, N_r * 334)` with phases staggered, so the sum of transitions in any rolling second stays at most 3 (D.9); a tick is a digit-glyph substitution, never an inversion of a plate. The inspect card calls the same `perceived(ref)` as its wall gauge, so it lies exactly when the gauge lies, from stage 1 (HR-14, IA-38); the card frame is an anchor and violet appears only on the reading's glass (ART 4.6).
353	**Return, hand-off and the region gap governor** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: during RETURN the lying numeral keeps stepping on the same scheduler to `round(slew_value / lsb)` (it follows the returning needle and never jumps to the honest value) and switches to the honest grid only at CLEAR, at the next `HONEST_TICK_MS` boundary. A STALE numeral is derived from the *displayed* needle value: it follows the needle by ticks during ONSET and holds from arrival, never jumping to the zone centre while the needle is still short of it, and every numeral (TICK step included) is clamped to `[value_lo, value_hi]`. A **region-level gap governor** guarantees at least 334 ms between any two Filter-owned lying ticks in a region, across a change of `N_r` when a lie starts or ends: a lying tick due sooner is deferred to the earliest slot 334 ms after the previous one and never queued twice, so the spacing guarantee survives an `N_r` change mid-run (D.9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The governor defers **only Filter-owned lying ticks** and never an honest swap: the lying-to-honest switch at CLEAR lands on the **next HUD grid boundary** (the `HONEST_TICK_MS` grid is HUD-owned, tick-anchored and skip-only, so the HUD arbiter admits the switch at that boundary or skips it to the following one, and never delays it; the numeral keeps its last lying value until then). **Honest-swap accounting** (registry `hud_flash_budget`): in WEIGHTED mode honest digit swaps are exempt and take no slot in `N_r`; in STRICT (reduce-flashing on, the first-launch default) they are not exempt, each counts as one transition in the region window, and the HUD arbiter never defers a Filter lying tick, so when `N_r` lying ticks already fill the window (`N_r` 3 is 2.994 per second) the arbiter skips the honest swap to its next boundary.
354	*Why.* One readout at the 333 ms floor already equals the transition ceiling; `LIES_MAX` 4 would exceed it unscheduled (four readouts at 400 ms are 10 transitions per second). The trade-off at `N_r` 4 is a weaker continuous cadence (about 0.75 Hz): still never stopped, still distinguishable from an honest numeral. (R35 said "at least 333 ms"; the arithmetic puts the first compliant value at 334 and the registry entry is written from this text.)
355	*Edge notes.* Reduced motion never lowers the interval (PF-39). The area model (a digit substitution changes well under 1 % of a region's luminance) would permit more, and the conservative reading binds for HUD-layer readouts, where HR-13 is region-agnostic (OQ-PF-12).
356	
357	**PF-19. State glyph, glow sprite and machine sprite.**
358	*Rule.* Frames come from the module's **own sheet**: a SPRITE_SWAP shows one of the machine's own honest state frames (a rotor spinning on a stopped machine, a housing cracked on a whole one) and is eligible only where both honest frames exist (the content gate is Sanity's SN-16 plus Instruments and Derelict Authoring; a missing frame draws nothing at all, no frame, no gleam and no sound, and counts `lie_unrenderable`, E-PF-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. "Cracked" is a `mach_*` state frame, never a `trail_*` hairline. The lamp-housing glow sprite lie swaps an unlit appearance frame that cannot read as a lantern pool (ART Principle 3). **Onset** is the mirror of return: the gleam rises first over `SWAP_LEAD_S` `[PLACEHOLDER]` (3 s; range 2 to 6) and the frame cut follows (for the rotor the "cut" is the start of the cadence wind-up over `ROTOR_WINDUP_S`, D.17, never a jump to running cadence on frame one) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; from the cut the gleam breathes (`motion_mode` BREATH, the static-pair hue-independent mode, PF-15 table, D.5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. **Return** (art-director ruling, one rule by lie type): a *continuous-variable* frame (rotor cadence on a stopped machine) winds its cadence toward the honest cadence at a constant rate that includes `rm_ret` and snaps to it at a minimum cadence (`ROTOR_SNAP_FRAC`, D.17), with the gleam outliving the snap, so the return is invisible and a false state is never shown without its leak *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a *static-pair* frame (cracked or whole, lit or unlit) cuts back to the honest frame and the gleam decays on the glide-return schedule after the cut, so the leak outlives the false frame and a false frame is never shown without its leak. Identical for the three end types. The rotor cadence of a SPRITE_SWAP lie drifts and never settles to the honest rate (D.17). **Route** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a SPRITE_SWAP, static pair and rotor alike, is applied by writing the lying node's own frame or region (one write at the cut and one at the cut-back for a pair, the per-frame cadence for the rotor), which is inside PF-2's write set, is per instance and a hard cut by construction, and so has no dependency on spike S-1 and no place in the PF-43 shared-shader block.
359	*Why.* HD pixel art has no blended in-between sprite and a half-cracked housing is a machine state that does not exist; a frame cut is the native vocabulary of machine state change, but an *uncaused* cut with no leak is an unleaked lie.
360	*Edge notes.* The afterglow after a static-pair cut tells the player something changed back, a mild oracle accepted because it is identical for all end types and never says why. Two alternatives were proposed and are carried, not adopted: an ordered-dither dissolve (the shader-specialist: every output texel is exactly one of the two honest frames' texels, so the palette stays exact) and a crossfade (the technical-artist; rejected, it produces off-palette blended pixels). OQ-PF-3 owes the art-director and creative-director confirmation. (orchestrator ruling: art-director's split rule adopted; R16 left the choice open.)
361	
362	**PF-20. The sound signature and `FILTER_AUDIO_CLASSES`.**
363	*Rule.* The Filter owns the **id namespace** `FILTER_AUDIO_CLASSES` and the request semantics `(viewer, ref or position, intent in {ON, LEVEL(pm), OFF}, class)`; Adaptive Audio owns assets, mix, bus and ducking, and states whether audio can lie *(Adaptive Audio & Tells, designed, honours this rule, answering IDX:41 with "audio can lie only through the hallucination family the Perception Filter requests for one viewer, every member of which carries an audible leak")*. MVP ids: `FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE` (needle, readout, card, glyph) and `FA_LIE_SIG_SPRITE` (housing, machine); VS-A: `FA_PHANTOM_MOVE`, `FA_PHANTOM_PRESENCE`. The request goes ON on the first ACTIVE frame (so it is requested no later than the first visible frame, HR-5; D.15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, LEVEL carries the lie's SOUND amplitude `amp_snd` (the unbreathed leak amplitude, per mille of `AMP_MAX_PM`, 0 to 1000; D.5, D.15), and OFF at CLEAR *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R8)*. The ids are **lint-disjoint** from the Graph's witness `acoustic` classes, Attention's tell family and Horror's sub-tell. Never altered, faked or added: the human voice and chat, the P1 proximity cue (physically real, played on every client), consequence-channel sounds, tell audio. Silent by requirement: the outline fringe, a stage transition, a recovery, a debunk, an expiry.
364	**Level contract: a quiet, slow breath, never a constant tone** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R8)*. No full-frame flash on any layer. Every Filter source is amplitude-continuous, **except the rise-only onset step** (0 to `floor_eff` on the first ACTIVE frame, SNV-13: a single-direction change on one gleam element, followed by no fall for at least half a breath period because a lie's gleam breath starts at its trough, D.8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and its modelled opposing-pair magnitude inside any rolling second stays under 10 % at the patch level and far under it at the region level (D.11; the ramps are monotone, the breath is a raised cosine whose turning points are at least 2 s apart), and the verification is a 60 s flash scan at stage 3 at the **largest field** (zoom 1x on 2160p, 36 times the 640x360 area).

445	*Edge notes.* Reduce-flashing is a separate toggle from reduced motion; Filter ramps are already flash-free, so it changes nothing here (PF-39).

447	**PF-33. No clean frame.**
448	*Rule.* The first RUNNING frame after LOADING, and the first frame after any `force_stage` or `force_level`, is presented **already filtered**: envelopes are set to their targets (`hard_start`), lies are drawn at the formula's value for the restored `lie_tau` with full leak from frame one, and `perceived` is answerable before the first RUNNING frame (Sanity rebuilds `sanity.perception` in `post_restore`, SN-23). No fade-in from clean. Glide and breath *phase* and the slew state may differ after restore; **while a lie is ACTIVE** its presence, kind, leak and displayed value (by PF-11) do not: the first frame shows the formula's value, which equals the pre-save value except for any slew gap that was still closing at the save (D.3), and a return in progress at the save is not restored (the entry had already left `sanity.perception`; E-PF-5). Counter `first_frame_filtered`.
449	*Why.* "One unfiltered frame would be a free oracle" (SN-23); AC-SL-124: "the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` must already be presented through the Perception Filter for the restored sanity level - the black hold covers any rebuild". 450	
451	**PF-34. Unseen lies and no leak culling.**
452	*Rule.* A listed lie is drawn whenever its surface is on screen and lit; there is no "seat away" special case; its trajectory is a function of sim time and reappears at the correct point. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP; Sanity now lists away entries, SN-23 `away`)* Sanity keeps an entry listed while the seat is in another compartment (`away` true), so a lie seen through an open door, from a hatch or at a zoomed-out field is one continuous lie: no ONSET, no RETURN, no CLEAR, no sound OFF or new ON, and no change to `amp`, `leak_modes`, wander or breath when the seat crosses a hatch. A RETURN begun by a compartment change would give the test "walk out of the room; if the gauge settles it was lying", an end-of-lie signature that PF-G9 and SNV-11 forbid. S3 state and the RETURN follower of a ref that is off screen advance on elapsed `present_time` by scalar arithmetic (no draw or shader work; the follower closes min(gap, R_ret x elapsed)), so a lie that ended while its surface was off screen is, when next drawn, exactly where an on-screen return would have put it (finished unless seen inside its return window); on the first drawn frame after an off-screen interval the ONSET/HOLD slew is re-latched with `hard_start` (D.3) so it equals the formula. At far zoom (the large field) level-of-detail may reduce amplitude *detail* (breath sampling rate only; the wander amplitude and frequency are never reduced, D.4), never remove a leak mode. Counts are bounded by `LIES_MAX`, not by the field, so zooming out multiplies nothing.
453	*Why.* "A culled leak is an unleaked lie" (OQ-SN-17 answered; SN-15 L-L). (orchestrator ruling R17.)

455	**PF-35. Frame order and latency.**
456	*Rule.* In the render callback the Filter runs **after** the Avatar Presenter and **before** Lighting reads the decoy list in the same frame. Dirty-mark in the notification, draw in the render callback (PIPE PR-8). A change in SIM reaches pixels after up to one sanity run (`SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR` 12 ticks = 0.2 s) plus one frame (D.16): stage steps and entry appearance and removal; lies and ramps then evolve on their own clocks.
457	*Why.* Accepted and stated in Game Feel. (orchestrator ruling R26.)
458	
459	**PF-36. Anchors that never shift.**
460	*Rule.* The chest point, beams, character sprites, hand tools, the HUD frame, the true reveal radius and **camera framing (position, zoom, rotation, offset)** are never written. No lie produces a jolt, zoom or shake (a camera jolt from Horror is Horror's and the Pipeline's, not the Filter's). The camera framing joins the never-shift anchor list (art-bible Corollary refresh, row 13).

content.thinking:
I'm examining PF-34 more closely: when a return happens off-screen then gets drawn again, the slew re-latches with hard_start, which forces it to the clamped target value — but I need to check how a pending slew gap during truth steps interacts with that re-latch.

There's also D.3's `s` latching behavior: it uses the direction from entry and the static record, which stays pure, but if a record holds multiple alarm intervals, the chosen interval closest to u_true at that frame could differ before and after a restore. That's a minor edge case the MVP dial handling can tolerate.

Next I want to move on to PF-37 through PF-46, then look at States and Transitions, and Interactions.

1160	## Edge Cases
1161	
1162	Every case states the exact outcome and the reason. Ids `E-PF-n` are cited by the rules and formulas (E-PF-3 by PF-14 and S3, E-PF-5 by PF-12 and PF-33, E-PF-46 by D.14). "Falls back to truth" means PF-44: the affected surface draws the honest path and a counter moves; a Filter fault never reaches the simulation or a TRUTH node.
1163	
1164	### Lie start, hold and end
1165	
1166	- **If a lie is accepted but its re-check fails or it is debunked while PENDING** *(E-PF-1)*: the entry never appears in `sanity.perception`, so nothing is drawn and `perceived` stays on the honest path (no pre-onset hint, SN-16). The Filter has no PENDING state of its own; this is why a debunk during the 2 to 5 s delay leaves no trace at all.
1167	- **If a debunk (`field_check`) lands at ACTIVE `lie_tau` 0.1 s** *(E-PF-2)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the entry leaves with `disc_end` about 0.1 deg, already under `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, so the unified RETURN follower of D.5 has no discrepancy tail (`amp_cand` is 0) and `amp_end` 400 falls at `R_AMP` 266.7 pm/s to exactly 0 in `LEAK_FADE_S` 1.5 s; the needle is already within `LEAK_EPS_DEG` of the truth, but the record stays RETURN, with `lie_id` held and the gleam fading, and CLEAR (the later of the discrepancy, the amplitude and the wander fade) arrives at `WANDER_BLEND_S` 3.0 s, when `motion_mode` returns to HONEST without an event. The earlier text left RETURN while the violet fade and the sound were still running, which put a gleam on an honest record. The first-frame bound of D.1 (at most 0.1 deg) means a lie that ends this early was never visibly displaced, but it did carry its gleam and its sound request, so it was never an unleaked lie.
1168	- **If a new lie starts on a ref whose previous lie is still in RETURN** *(E-PF-3)*: the new lie **starts from its own formula** (discrepancy against the true value is 0 at `lie_tau` 0); the displayed value does **not** continue from the return's value, so an ACTIVE lie's displayed value never depends on presentation-local return state and PF-11 and PF-33 hold. The single slew state (D.3) closes the residual gap between the in-flight return value and the new lie's target at a rate of at most `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` (8.33 pm/s at 240 deg): no snap, and after a restore the displayed value equals the formula from the first frame. The gleam steps up on the frame the new entry appears (from the RETURN value to `floor_eff + (AMP_MAX_PM - floor_eff) x g(disc)`, a rise of up to about 400 per mille) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. That step is accepted: it is a rise (the safe direction, never an unleaked moment), the new lie must carry its full leak from frame one (SN-15 L-L, SNV-13), and it cannot make a flash pair, because the other half of a pair would be the preceding return decline, which is below 0.10 per second by the D.6 coupling (D.11). Sanity's `LIE_GAP_S` normally prevents the case; it is defensive.
1169	- **If EXPIRED, INVALIDATED and DEBUNKED each remove an entry at the same `disc_end` (48 deg)** *(E-PF-4)*: the `displayed_pm(t)` and `amp(t)` series are bit-identical across the three; no verdict flash, relief cue or sound sting. The Filter sees only that the entry left (PF-12), so the end type cannot become an oracle (SN-16, SNV-11, AC-SN-153).
1170	- **If a save is loaded, or LOADING happens, while a lie is in RETURN** *(E-PF-5)*: the return track is presentation-local and is dropped; the entry had already left `sanity.perception`, so nothing is ACTIVE, and the first RUNNING frame (behind the black hold) shows the true value. This is not a clean-frame oracle (no lie is active to hide). The residual tell, "loading cleared the tail", is accepted (OQ-PF-9 answered: ended entries are not retained, loading clears the tail).
1171	- **If `sanity.perception` holds two entries with the same `subject_ref` for the viewer** *(E-PF-6)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: only the lowest `start_run` draws, ties broken by the lowest `lie_id`, then (last resort) entry order, ascending ledger `slot` as published *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1; defensive only: Sanity allows one live lie per subject)*; the other contributes no pixels and no sound; counter `lie_collisions`; no leak is lost because the winner carries its own (PF-46). Sanity's pre-draw gate enforces at most one live lie per (seat, subject_ref) (SN-16; registry `sanity.ledger`), so this tie-break is a defensive fallback.
1172	- **If the true value moves through a FALSE_OK or FALSE_FAIL target** *(E-PF-7)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the aim distance reaches 0 (the true value is inside the aim point's zone interval) and the displayed needle meets the truth; `amp` stays at its ACTIVE value (never below `floor_eff`, 400 at stages 0 to 1) until Sanity's re-check removes the entry within one run (0.2 s), after which the RETURN follower of D.5 applies. The needle meets the truth for at most that window; the gleam and the sound stay on throughout *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the amplitude does not step when the aim distance reaches 0: it falls only through the `R_AMP_ACT` follower).
1173	- **If the true value steps by 500 pm in one Graph step (`apply_damage`, a repair) while a lie is ACTIVE** *(E-PF-8)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: GLIDE carries its offset with the truth (the target steps) and FALSE_* keeps the zone; the displayed value follows through the slew at `R_act` 8.33 pm/s and does not snap or settle (SNV-11, SNV-23), **except where the `DISC_CAP_PM` clamp binds**: the slew is held within 400 pm of the truth, so after a step or ramp larger than the cap the needle moves faster than `R_act` once, to the cap, and stays there (D.3; a bounded exception, OQ-PF-40). The discrepancy and the leak grow for as long as the slew lags, at worst about 48 s; when the step moves the truth **toward** a GLIDE needle and `disc` collapses by up to 400 pm in one frame, the gleam amplitude falls only at `R_AMP_ACT` (266.7 pm/s, 0.0776 of luminance per second), so the step is not visible as a gleam event and tells the player nothing about where the truth moved *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a step in the **true** needle is honest and is not the Filter's (Instruments apply their settle only when `motion_mode` is HONEST, which an ACTIVE lie is not). A truth ramp of 100 pm/s pins the discrepancy at -400 pm after 5.5 s (AC-PF-114).
1174	- **If the subject of a lie is destroyed mid-glide (`true_value` no longer resolves)** *(E-PF-9)*: the entry leaves (INVALIDATED); the ref draws nothing (the instrument is gone), there is no return animation, and the per-lie state is freed the same frame. A Filter datum that throws or goes missing falls back to truth (PF-44).
1175	- **If the truth sits at or near a dial stop in the departure direction, so the live clamp leaves less than `D_VIS_MIN_DEG`** *(E-PF-10)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `D_eff` is a per-lie constant and is not reduced; the target is clamped live to `[W_M, 1000 - W_M]` (D.3), so displayed-minus-true is smaller than usual for as long as the truth stays there. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)* The departure direction is the published one (`s = d x c_dial`, D.3); the clamp shrinks the departure and never reverses it to the other side of the dial (with the truth inside the last `W_M` before the stop the target sits at the clamp edge, under `W_M` from the truth), and Sanity's pre-draw gate (a) is direction-specific (room toward the published direction, OQ-PF-38). The lie is still drawn with its gleam, its sound and its **wander, the needle's hue-independent motion mode, which the clamp never removes** (the needle never pins at a stop: a pinned needle rests); `lie_short_reach` counts once per lie. A needle lie therefore always has GLEAM plus a motion mode. It is a weak lie, not an unleaked one, and Sanity's pre-draw gate should refuse a subject with no room (OQ-PF-38).
1176	- **If the calibration record is missing or `needle_len_px` is below the 14.3 art-px eligibility floor (`NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` default 16)** *(E-PF-11)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a missing record draws nothing for the ref and counts `lie_unrenderable` (a build failure for any kind listed in `lie_targets.json`, PF-6 vi). A short needle cannot give a needle glide (`28.6 / 14 = 2.04 > GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`) and a gleam with a sound has no hue-independent motion mode, so **the surface is not lied on** (the honest path, `lie_unrenderable`) unless the same ref has a visible digit mechanism whose TICK, or STALE with the gleam breath, is then its motion mode (PF-15 table); a build lint excludes such a gauge from `lie_targets.json` (requested of Sanity's data, OQ-PF-38). The earlier text kept "the gleam and the readout mode", which for a gauge with no numeral meant a gleam and a sound only.
1177	- **If a SPRITE_SWAP lie targets a machine whose sheet lacks the opposite honest frame** *(E-PF-12)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: no swap is drawn (the Filter never invents or blends a frame) and, because a gleam on an unchanged sprite is a violet mark on an honest surface with no motion mode, **no gleam and no sound are drawn either**: the ref takes the honest path, counter `lie_unrenderable`, log `SPRITE_FRAME_MISSING`. The content gate (SN-16 plus Instruments and Derelict Authoring) is the first defence; the lie is lost whole and never half-drawn.
1178	- **If a lie's onset lands during an Instruments settle in progress** *(E-PF-62)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: Instruments clears its settle and tremor triple on the first non-HONEST frame and the drawn needle moves to `displayed_pm` by at most the settle's current deviation (In-World Instruments IW:243, checkpoint ruling C14). That deviation is bounded by the honest step that started the settle, which is one LS-20 quantum (for example 20 permille of range for a store) except after a Graph step such as `apply_damage`, where it can be larger; an honest needle at rest has none, and the first lie is drawn on a fault-free subject at rest (SN-16). The one-frame move is accepted: it ends a settle that was already running rather than starting an uncaused move, the leak (gleam at `floor_eff`, the sound request) is on from the same frame, and any tremor in progress is blended out by `tremor_weight_pm` over `TREMOR_BLEND_S`. The Filter adds no additive tail (it brushes PF-17, OQ-IW-6).

1180	### Stage, ramp and QA flags
1181	
1182	- **If the stage drops while an envelope is mid-ramp** *(E-PF-13)*: the envelope reverses from its current value with its rate re-latched (D.7), so the return takes `STAGE_RAMP_S` (8 s) from any value (from 0.5 at 0.0625 per second, from 0.375 at 0.047 per second); no restart at 0, no relief cue; ACTIVE lies run on (a stage change never ends a lie, SN-16). 1183	- **If the stage flaps around a threshold** *(E-PF-14)*: the hysteresis (`STAGE_HYST` 2000 mSU) and the dwell (`STAGE_DWELL_RUNS` 25, 5 s) keep reversals at least 5 s apart; the envelope integrates the net direction continuously, so between flips it moves by at most 5/8 of the current step (5 s of an 8 s transition), and no opposing pair can fall inside 1 s (D.11).
1184	- **If `force_stage` jumps the stage from 0 to 3, or sets any stage** *(E-PF-15)*: `hard_start`: every envelope is set to its target on the first rendered frame with no ramp (rim and bleed at their stage-3 gains), every ACTIVE lie is drawn at the formula's value for the current `lie_tau`, and counter `first_frame_filtered` moves. QA flags exist only in debug builds (SN-28); two flips inside 1 s are outside the flash model and outside release.
1185	- **If `force_level` changes the sanity level with a lie ACTIVE** *(E-PF-16)*: as E-PF-15; the lie's presence, kind and leak are unchanged (the entry is Sanity's), only the stage-bound envelopes jump; the picture is never presented clean for one frame (PF-33).

1211	- **If `perceived(ref, P)` is called with a PlayerId that is not the local seat** *(E-PF-32)*: the honest record returns (`displayed` equals the true value, `leak_amplitude_pm` 0, `motion_mode` HONEST, `lie_id` 0); counter `remote_queries`; never an error (PF-10). Answering from replicated data would let a client compute another's lies.
1212	- **If the viewer is themself `tell_on`** *(E-PF-33)*: the victim tell of **other** seats is rendered normally (absence would be a self-sign, PF-28); nothing about the viewer's own body changes.
1213	- **If `harm_eligible` sets mid-stride (VS-B)** *(E-PF-34)*: on the next rendered frame every other bound seat's body is substituted by a horror rig at the true position and driven by the true velocity (hard cut, no morph, no glimpse); the true beam stays anchored to the true chest point and the true voice plays (PF-29).
1214	- **If `harm_eligible` clears (immediate, no dwell on exit)** *(E-PF-35)*: the rig is replaced by the crewmate body on the next rendered frame, again a hard cut; the monsterised rig did not draw the held tool's body, while the tool's true emission VFX stayed (OQ-SN-26 recommendation).
1215	- **If `tell_on(B)` and `harm_eligible(A)` both hold** *(E-PF-36)*: one fringe (the rig's contour with `leak` above 0) is drawn, never two (SNV-17).
1216	- **If a substituted or phantom rig is rendered with `leak` 0** *(E-PF-37)*: the build lint fails (HE-40, HE:1189); at runtime the Filter raises it to the minimum visible leak and counts `leak_repaired`; a rig with no violet contour would be an unleaked lie.
1217	- **If two viewers share one machine (VS-B)** *(E-PF-38)*: seat A with a lie on gauge G sees D.3's value, seat B sees honest; the hash includes `viewer`, so their wander and breath sequences differ even for the same `lie_key`.
1218	- **If a lie is ACTIVE on a gauge while an endogenous breach alarm fires** *(E-PF-39)*: the lie neither shows nor suppresses the warning mark, the alarm sweep or any tell (anchors); `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (10 s, Graph) and "alarm class never first" are Sanity's and the Graph's gates; the Filter's draw is unaffected (LS-13).
1219	- **If a lamp-housing glow sprite lies** *(E-PF-40)*: only the appearance frame swaps; the real lamp light, the floor pool and `lux` are unchanged and TRUTH (AC-SN-122); a housing lit over a cold floor is the whole lie.
1220	
1221	### Degenerate strategies and settings
1222	
1223	- **If the player zooms to 1x to survey the ship for liars** *(E-PF-41)*: lies on screen and lit show every mode at their normal strength; nothing extra is revealed (no extra leak, no count), and the number of lies is bounded by `LIES_MAX`; zooming in cannot hide a leak either (widths scale with `k`).
1224	- **If the player mutes audio, or has no audio device** *(E-PF-42)*: the lie keeps the gleam and the glide (two modes); the player's mute is not a Filter event, and the sound request is still emitted (Audio decides playback).
1225	- **If the player turns on reduced motion mid-lie** *(E-PF-43)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `rm` is latched per lie at activation and at `hard_start`, so an in-flight lie keeps its time axis and new lies use the scaled one (`D_eff` is identical either way, so no lie is smaller); the wander amplitude and frequency are never scaled, the digit tick is never lowered below `LIE_TICK_MS`, and the breath stays (HR-7). The return uses `rm_ret = max(rm, RM_RETURN_FLOOR)`, so the assertion `rm_ret x GLIDE_RETURN_RATE >= rm x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` holds and the reduced-motion return takes at most about 1.2 times the normal one.
1226	- **If the player runs an OS colour filter or is hue-blind** *(E-PF-44)*: no global remap or daltonization is applied (HR-10); the glide and the breathing carry the lie without hue; a hue-removed tester still finds the liar by motion and by sound (AC-SN-154).
1227	- **If the player stares at the pause screen's frame to find the liar** *(E-PF-45)*: the paused frame contains the same leaks as the live frame and nothing more; a still needle shows no motion, but the gleam, the edge and the housing frames remain, so pausing neither hides nor reveals a lie.
1228	
1229	### Numeric, content and build-time cases
1230	
1231	- **If a `lie_id`, `ref_key` or `viewer` exceeds 32 bits** *(E-PF-46)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1)*: it is masked to 32 bits before mixing (D.14); the lie key is forced non-zero (`lie_id` 0 or 2^32 maps to 0xFFFFFFFF; unreachable from a conforming entry); a collision only changes presentation phase, never a displayed value or a leak.
1232	- **If the dead zones leave no legal breath period** *(E-PF-47)*: the draw clamps deterministically to the nearer zone boundary inside the 4000 to 6000 ms band; a zone wider than the band is a boot assertion failure (a configuration error).
1233	- **If a node has no `PerceptionTag`, or a CORRUPTIBLE tag's `lie_surface_id` is absent from `lie_targets.json`** *(E-PF-48)*: an untagged node is TRUTH and counts `tag_defaults_applied` once per node per session (never an error); the missing id fails the build and at runtime the node is treated as TRUTH (PF-4, PF-6).
1234	- **If an entry arrives with empty `leak_modes`, or with `leak_modes` that lacks the GLEAM bit** *(E-PF-49)*: a debug build asserts; a release build draws GLEAM and GLIDE for an empty entry, **adds GLEAM** to any entry that arrives without it (keeping the modes it did carry), and counts `leak_repaired` once per lie, so neither an unleaked lie nor a palette-silent lie is ever drawn (PF-15).
1235	- **If the stage-3 worst case would exceed `D_FX_ADDED_MAX` draws (neither the instance-parameter path nor the MultiMesh overlay is available, path 3 of D.12)** *(E-PF-50)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the lies that do not fit are not drawn at all (the oldest survive: lowest `start_run`, then lowest `lie_id` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*); counter `filter_draws_dropped` counts those lies; every lie that is drawn keeps GLEAM **and** its motion mode, so the invariant of PF-15 holds on the fallback and is linted (AC-PF-108). The earlier claim that "the glide and the sound need no draw" was false for the static-pair classes, whose motion mode is the gleam breath, and the sound is not a motion mode. Surviving draws per stage: D.12.
1236	- **If per-instance shader parameters are unavailable or capped on a tested GPU or backend** *(E-PF-51)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the gleam transport falls to the MultiMesh overlay (D.12 path 2, spike S-1c) and, if that fails its batching, ordering or light-mask test, to path 3 and then to the recorded reduced lie set (PF-42); `self_modulate` is **not** a fallback (it cannot draw an edge-only gleam and would take the host's only modulate channel); spike S-1a decides before the rules depend on it `[UNV]`.
1237	- **If the container material slot is null** *(E-PF-52)*: the Filter reports `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT` and container `NOT_USED`; `filter_pass_disabled` shows no red (X13); `NO_MASK` is reserved for a route that expects a mask and has none.
1238	- **If a pipe sheet pixel is both silhouette edge and emission or chevron** *(E-PF-53)*: emission wins (the bleed is multiplied by `1 - emission`); chevron shape, pattern, speed and direction are never touched (PF-24).
1239	- **If the rim band's beam is occluded by a wall 3 tiles away** *(E-PF-54)*: the band stops at the occluder cut and never follows the shadow edge; no violet appears on the far side of the wall at any ladder step (a free wall-hack otherwise); the one-frame pose lag of Lighting's beam is a registration failure, so the Filter reads the same-frame published pose (PF-23, PF-35).
1240	- **If every leak parameter of a material is at its rest value** *(E-PF-55)*: the output is bit-identical to the unmodified material (pass-through exactness, PF-43); a TRUTH_PX node carries the shared material at rest only (PF-6 ii).
1241	- **If `rate_floor` exceeds `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG` (a needle shorter than about 14.3 px) or the truth lies outside the clamp range `[W_M, 1000 - W_M]` (the old negative `room_deg`)** *(E-PF-56)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the first makes the needle ineligible (E-PF-11); the second clamps the target live (E-PF-10): the lie keeps its gleam, its sound and its wander, and `lie_short_reach` moves.
1242	- **If the slew is pinned at `DISC_CAP_PM` when the lie ends** *(E-PF-64)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: RETURN starts from the pinned value; the follower closes the gap at `rm_ret x GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` (a 400 pm gap is 96 deg, at most 32 s at `rm` 1.0), `amp_end` is 1000 and the series is the 48-deg series of D.5 stretched by the longer tail; the cap applies to the follower as well, so a truth that moves away cannot widen the gap past 400 pm.
1243	- **If `N_r` changes mid-run (a lying readout starts or ends in the region, or the lying-to-honest switch lands at CLEAR)** *(E-PF-65)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `T_tick` re-evaluates at the next tick and the region gap governor defers any lying tick due less than 334 ms after the previous one to the earliest slot 334 ms later (never queued twice), so no closed second in the region holds more than three Filter transitions across the change; the lying-to-honest switch at CLEAR lands on the next HUD grid boundary and is the HUD arbiter's to admit or skip (AC-PF-75b, AC-PF-75c) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
1244	- **If a configuration violates a build assertion (`STAGE_RAMP_S` below its floor, `GLIDE_RETURN_RATE` below `GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG`, `LEAK_D_FULL_DEG` at or below `LEAK_EPS_DEG`, the never-rest amplitude bound, the flash bound on amplitude falls, D.5/D.6)** *(E-PF-57)*: the boot check fails with the assertion's name (a data error, not a runtime state); a tuning knob can therefore never silently leave its derived safe range.
1245	- **If two fringes are visible at once (the rim band and a crewmate outline)** *(E-PF-58)*: they use different hashed breath sequences (different `(subject or rim, seat)` keys), so they do not beat in phase; neither is locked to `tell_beat`, the alarm sweep or the voice-activity cue (PF-30, D.8).
1246	- **If `CLASSES_ENABLED` clears class (b) mid-session** *(E-PF-59)*: the entries leave `sanity.perception` and every lie takes the D.6 return path (SN-16 INVALIDATED), never a pop.
1247	- **If a client joins mid-session or a seat changes owner (VS-B)** *(E-PF-60)*: the tell and outline envelopes of the joining viewer start at their targets (`hard_start`), because a fade-in from clean would be a free oracle for that viewer; the joining seat's own `sanity.perception` is OWNER_PRIVATE and arrives by the owner's own restore path.
1248	- **If the Debug Overlay is on** *(E-PF-61)*: it reads `true_value` and `perceived` for the same ref and the Filter's counters; the Filter's draw path is unchanged (the overlay is a DIAGNOSTIC subscriber, never an accessibility feature, absent from release builds), and it can show deliberate corruption beside real desync because `state_hash` excludes the perceived channel.

I'm checking these ACs against the spec: the wander amplitude, the displayed_pm formula within the slew gap, and the S3 condition all look consistent, though I'm now flagging a potential discrepancy between N_G_REGION values and what D.11 describes.

I verify the N_G_REGION formula against several resolution tiers — Deck top rung, 1080p, 2160p, and 640x360 — and each computation checks out against the stated caps of 10, 18, and 33, including the k=3 edge case giving 7. I also confirm the region-area calculations across multiple resolutions and k values all match expected pixel counts, but notice AC-PF-12 conflates two scenarios regarding the 0.05 cap beyond a certain threshold.

The AC-PF-12 text conflicts with itself: it claims a 0.0725 figure as the testing value while simultaneously asserting a 0.05 post-cap bound, but the post-cap value is actually 0.0484, meaning the exception clause it introduces is unnecessary and the AC needs rewriting for clarity. There's also an unresolved tension about whether a dropped static-pair lie at stage 3 is still being counted as live in Sanity's ledger despite taking the "honest path" through the filter.

This lie is also invisible to Sanity until the view zooms, since the draw reappears on zoom-out — making zoom-toggling an oracle for detecting hidden lies, which seems to violate the spirit of PF-34's guarantee that zoom changes don't add or remove entries, even though PF-34 technically only covers entries rather than draws. Since this only manifests in a niche 640x360-at-k=3 config that Pipeline may not even support, I'm thinking this belongs as a RECOMMENDED note suggesting either barring that ladder rung or redefining the cap as a per-window constant rather than per-rung — and I want to check how OQ-PF-45 and the Pipeline-owned text already address this before finalizing.

Checking the acceptance criteria tied to HONEST_GRID_TICKS, the tick math works out correctly. Verifying whether AC-PF-75c's "at most 3 lying/honest transitions per rolling second" constraint is actually satisfiable given the arbiter never defers lying ticks — this seems to conflict with HUD's GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS rule, something flagged previously as RECOMMENDED rather than BLOCKING, so I'll note it as a bonus check since the blockers file only lists two BLOCKING items. The remaining criteria (tester scoring thresholds, glide ranges, flash-region captures) all look testable and fine, so now I'm moving on to review the discharge section, the gaps/untestable items, and the open questions.

**HS-46. The failed-write notice and the first-frame line.** *Rule.* **Notice:** a 16 x 16 Paper White "record slot" glyph on a chamfered Ground plate at the suit panel's edge, with the one phrase (string key `notice_save_failed`, English placeholder "The game could not write its record.") in the reading face, shown only while Save/Load reports the failed-write escalation: `save_status` reads `FAILED` on every failed write (sl:739), and the notice is raised only after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` (registry: 3, range 1-10, Save/Load) consecutive failures (sl:739, sl:1006). **The HUD counts nothing**: it reads a Save/Load-published escalation flag (`fail_escalated`, bool, a Save/Load SL-21 host-local read, registry `save_status` companion_read; true from the 3rd consecutive failed write until the next `WRITTEN`); persistent, non-modal, no animation, no cause, cleared by the next `WRITTEN`; no Alarm Red, no Flesh, no Violet; never lie-capable. There is **no per-write glyph**: UI-1 is retired, `STATUS_WRITTEN_HOLD_TICKS` stays retired, and no sound, text or mark announces an autosave. **First-frame line (UI-7):** one plain reading-face line ("Newest record unreadable. Continuing from the one before it.", placeholder) on a Ground plate stacked at the panel's edge above the notice slot, on the first `RUNNING` frame after a fallback load, for `UI7_DWELL_S` 8 `[PH]` (range 5-15) and then a cut; if the Chart Table already shows it under Continue, the HUD shows nothing. **Second trigger, `DEATH_STUB` (user ruling D15 / D84):** on the first `RUNNING` frame after a restore whose `restore_reason` is `DEATH_STUB`, the same slot shows one plain ship-log line (string key `line_record_restored`, English placeholder "Restored from the last record."; no death wording, no cause, no count, no summary of what was lost) for `UI7_DWELL_S`, then a cut. The Chart Table shows nothing at a death restore (the restore is in-game and automatic, SL-7), so the HUD always shows it. **Both at once:** if the fallback flag is also set, the fallback line is shown and the death line is not (the fallback line already says the game is continuing from an earlier record; one line at a time, no queue). `restore_reason` stays a request: it keys this one line and alters nothing else (HS-53) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. (orchestrator ruling: the ui-programmer's "centre-low" placement is dropped; both meta plates share the panel's edge so nothing new enters the bottom-centre band.) *Why.* Save/Load's UI-10 and UI-7; the Chart Table's ASK-CT-5 agrees.

**HS-47. The flash arbiter (`hud_flash_budget`).** *Rule.* One arbiter counts luminance events per rolling second across the HUD. **Its clock is the committed tick `T`** (window `(T - TICK_RATE, T]`): `present_time` drives animation, not the budget; an event that originates in render time (a focus becoming stable, a press) is stamped with the tick current at that render frame, and while the kernel is `PAUSED` `T` does not advance, so no deferrable event is admitted while paused. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The event inventory** (every HUD luminance event, with its class; the events added by the review are marked *new*): **clock-locked, never delayed:** mark leading edges (at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0`); honest-numeral **grid boundaries** at `T mod HONEST_GRID_TICKS == 0` at which at least one displayed digit actually changes (a boundary with no displayed change is not an event, so the 2 events/s is a ceiling reached only while the numerals are falling), which are **skip-only**: drawn on their own tick or skipped, never delayed. **Never rescheduled by the HUD:** lying-digit ticks (the Filter's schedule). **Follow the honest source state, counted, never deferred:** source-state hue cuts (HSV-4, L-5: a glyph or arc band changing between its loop hue and Graphite lit). **Source-state swap** *(new, re-review)*: the strip's `breath_src` swap (HS-12, HSV-42), counted once, never deferred, like a hue cut. **give_up plate show-start and hide** (HS-42(b), HSV-43) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: they follow `confirm_view.give_up_live`; the show is never deferred (it must appear on the first DOWNED frame), a hide is immediate and counts under the orphan rule if its show lies before the window; re-shows are spaced by `since_last_show >= PROMPT_MIN_CYCLE_TICKS` (EC-HS-57), so the plate contributes at most 3 show-starts per second; in WEIGHTED mode the show-start is treated as a prompt show-start for the `flash_weight_pm` exemption (neither counted nor deferred below `FLASH_AREA_EXEMPT_PM`), in STRICT it is counted and may overrun (`HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN` recorded, nothing dropped). **Orphan transitions** *(new, re-review)*: a plate hide whose show-start lies before the window, and a mark OFF edge whose ON edge does, are counted once in `N(w)` for the windows that contain them (they are known only when they occur, so they are non-deferrable and may overrun, D.2). **A counted mark event is an actual change in the drawn luminance of a mark slot, not a scheduled boundary** *(new, re-review)*: three cases were missing from the inventory. (1) A **leading edge** at `T mod BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS == 0` counts only when the slot is active and was drawn OFF (outline to fill); at a tick where the mark is already drawn ON (held solid by STRICT or reduced motion, held by pause, or bridged after a resume, HS-23) the natural edge changes nothing and is **not** counted. (2) A **mid-phase appearance**: an inactive slot becoming active draws the filled square at once when it is solid (STRICT, reduced motion) or when the live phase is inside the duty (D.4), which is one counted, non-deferrable event at that tick; in the pulsing case outside the duty it draws the OFF outline (a luminance change, one event) and the next leading edge is then counted normally. (3) The **pause-induced edge** (entering the hold from an OFF phase) is one event, per HS-23. The scheduled mark entry in `W(t)` is conditional: it exists only for a slot that is active **and** p

**HS-48. One `Theme`, one component set.** *Rule.* The HUD owns the single Godot `Theme` (`ui_theme_main`) and the shared components: keycap, Ground plate, chamfered bezel, focus bracket, linear bar with needle-mark, tabular-numeral label, gleam-on-glass helper and nine-slice bezels. They are specified in `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`, which the HUD's UX spec lands first; the HUD's UX spec lands first and the Chart Table cites it (dependency lateral, Soft). The shared component is the look only; each owner keeps its behaviour (the HUD's release drain, HS-42; the Chart Table's snap on abort, CT-22; Chart Table C19). *Why.* The HUD has the more constrained components (7-px numerals, 16-px glyphs, opaque plates) and is the earlier MVP surface. That makes AC-PF-75c effectively unsatisfiable as written, so the prior RECOMMENDED fix wasn't actually applied, and I'm drafting a corrected rewrite that separates the consecutive-skip bound from the lying-only sum constraint and explicitly accounts for overrun via HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN.

1697	## UI Requirements
1698	
1699	**The Perception Filter has no UI of its own and owns no HUD, instrument, card, prompt, menu or settings node.** It is a data and material supplier: it returns what a surface should display for the local peer, and it draws marks on nodes that other systems own. The surfaces below are owned by **In-World Instruments & Inspect View**, **HUD & Suit Layer**, **Debug Overlay (True Values)**, **Accessibility Settings** and **Adaptive Audio & Tells**, all undesigned or in flight at the time of writing; Instruments, HUD, Debug Overlay and Adaptive Audio have since been designed and answer their rows (OQ-PF-29), and the Accessibility Settings row stays a *provisional* request. No sanity meter, bar, ring, number, icon or colour exists on any surface, at any stage (PF-38); no UX Flag is raised because no screen, widget or HUD element is added by this system.

Checking the file's scope and freshness, it's a large GDD (561KB) last updated 2026-10-28, with change receipts matching the expected cross-GDD fix pass. I'm cross-referencing the dependency list against the full registry — all existing GDDs are accounted for except Accessibility Settings and Co-op Session, which are undesigned and not blocking at this review tier. Both prior blockers appear resolved, pending sibling verification.

No findings rise to BLOCKING severity, but a few merit RECOMMENDED flags: an undefined off-screen sound amplitude variable, a truth-step rise issue, and a HUD acceptance criterion (AC-PF-75c) that conflicts with HS-47's honest-boundary rule — working through the timing math, the rolling-second sum of lying plus honest ticks seems to exceed the stated cap of 3 regardless of window alignment, suggesting the AC may be genuinely unsatisfiable as written.

Since this unsatisfiable AC was already flagged in a prior review and left unaddressed, and the fix is just a straightforward text correction rather than a logic change, I'm going to keep it rated RECOMMENDED while calling out that it's the most important item on the list.

For the rng_derive conflict, that stays RECOMMENDED since it's dormant. The OQ-PF-42 consumer drift issue also gets RECOMMENDED, but I want to mandate an epic-level gate since this is now the fourth time it's carried over and CD specifically asked about it — I should note that RM_GLIDE_SCALE 0.6 is stale across both Instruments and the HUD.

Now I'm weighing the zone gate discrepancy — 400 versus 200pm — where Sanity SN-23(b) only references 400 while Filter OQ-PF-38 item 3 calls for a minimum calculation. This looks like a genuine conflict between two existing GDDs over which value is authoritative, and I need to figure out which system actually owns the reach constants that publish D_eff capability.

Sanity's text claims it reads the Filter's registered constants, but it only actually uses D_MAX_FRAC_ARC — so I'll flag this as RECOMMENDED: at L_s=40s, the 200-400pm zone-edge distances pass Sanity's gate but then trigger a lies_zone_missed WARN, since D_eff for FALSE kinds at 40s computes to 48 degrees, which is 200pm.

The AC-PF-12 derived constraints table misreporting post-cap is a clear RECOMMENDED. Then there's the D.11 zoom-dependent drop case — I'm questioning whether it's truly oracle-worthy, since it only drops static-pair lies when zoomed to k=3 on a 640x360 window at stage 3 with the rim shipped, meaning a player would actually see a housing lie vanish upon zooming in. This conflicts with both PF-34's intent that a zoom change should never do this, and PF-15's principle that a drawn lie's leak is never reduced — except here the lie isn't drawn at all, so filter_draws_dropped only counts as a WARN. I'm debating whether to fold this into the same finding as the OQ-PF-45 flash/pipeline-stops-ladder issue or keep it as its own separate RECOMMENDED — leaning toward keeping it separate, framed as "zoom-dependent lie drop."

I'm now compiling a batch of smaller NICE-level findings — the D.6 variance row, E-PF-57 versus AC-49(g) versus Tuning, the PX-8 "Deck-class" wording, stale text in OQ-PF-38 item 3, the vague "undesigned or in flight" language in the UI Requirements intro, the SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM range inconsistency, vague AC-PF-66c wording, the D.3 multi-alarm latch not restoring exactly, and outdated text in OQ-PF-42 — plus a list of untestable AC rewrites to include with quoted text.

For the "ACTIVE rises instantaneous" finding, I'm noting the contradiction between the claim that rises are instantaneous and the Output Range statement that the rise-only onset step is the sole discontinuity in gleam amplitude. My fix is to add an R_AMP_RISE limit similar to the 266.7 pm/s rate while still preserving the "full leak from frame one" floor as a lower bound, rate-limiting rises above that floor, and applying a_env after hard_start — plus noting the off-screen amp_snd case.

Tallying roughly twelve findings total, I'm also checking the freshness metadata — both receipts show CHANGED, file modified 2026-10-28, content changed since the last logged hash. With zero BLOCKING issues and both prior blockers RESOLVED, I'm leaning toward a verdict of "APPROVED with minor revisions" or CONCERNS rather than NEEDS REVISION. I'll skip calling the advisor since this is a read-only review with a fixed output schema, and I've already completed the substantive analysis — time to produce the final output.

findings.section: Acceptance Criteria: AC-PF-75c; Open Questions: OQ-PF-44; sibling hud-and-suit-layer.md HS-47
findings.finding: AC-PF-75c cannot pass at the default setting. It requires 'the sum of lying and honest transitions in any rolling second is at most 3' and says 'every honest swap that the window cannot hold is skipped ... (skip-only, never delayed)'. With reduce-flashing ON (STRICT, the first-launch default) and N_r = 3 lying readouts (2.994 per second), the HUD's registered rule is 'a grid boundary is never skipped twice in a row (GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS 1)'. The boundary after a skip is admitted 'whatever waits'. So an honest swap is admitted about once per second, and some rolling window then holds 3 lying ticks plus 1 honest swap, which is 4. This was flagged as RECOMMENDED in the previous review and is unchanged. OQ-PF-44 still describes only the skip and says nothing of the two-skip bound or of `HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN`.
findings.fix: Rewrite the AC: 'GIVEN STRICT and N_r = 3 lying readouts plus one honest numeral in the region WHEN transitions are logged for 60 s THEN (a) no Filter lying tick is deferred or dropped by the arbiter and lying ticks stay at least 334 ms apart; (b) the lying-only count in any rolling second is at most 3; (c) an honest swap is skipped at most once in a row (GRID_MAX_CONSEC_SKIPS 1, HS-47) and the admitted swap may take a window to 4, recorded as HUD_FLASH_OVERRUN with nothing dropped; (d) the Filter governor logs no honest-swap deferral.' Make the same change in PF-18 'Honest-swap accounting' and OQ-PF-44.

findings.section: Formulas D.5 (ACTIVE follower) and D.11 / PF-32; Edge Cases E-PF-8
findings.finding: The text is internally contradictory. D.5 says 'rises are instantaneous, only falls are rate-limited' and 'rises stay instantaneous because they follow the glide, whose slope is at most 61 pm/s'. It also says 'the only discontinuity left in a gleam amplitude is the rise-only onset step', and PF-32 repeats that. But `disc` is computed from the lagging `slew_pm`, so a truth step is a second source of rises. A Graph step of 500 pm on a GLIDE needle with a small offset, or on a FALSE_* lie, moves `disc` by up to 400 pm in one frame. `a_cand` then jumps by up to 600 per mille, about 0.175 of relative luminance, in one frame. That is the 'the truth just moved' tell that limiting the falls was meant to remove. The previous review flagged the same point as RECOMMENDED and it is unchanged. D.11 and the 'only discontinuity' claims are therefore wrong as written.
findings.fix: Rate-limit rises as well: `a_env(t+dt) = clamp(a_cand, a_env - R_AMP_ACT*dt, a_env + R_AMP_RISE*dt)`, with R_AMP_RISE a PLACEHOLDER of 266.7 pm/s (equal to the fall bound, covered by assertion (m)). `hard_start` keeps `a_env := a_cand`, and the floor still holds from frame 1. Then add a rise vector to AC-PF-81 and AC-PF-19, and amend the 'only discontinuity' sentences in D.5, D.11 and PF-32. If rises are meant to stay instantaneous, drop the 61 pm/s justification and add the truth-step rise to D.11 as a second, accepted discontinuity with its flash bound.

findings.section: Detailed Rules PF-20 / PF-34 / D.15; Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-67
findings.finding: Underspecified now that away entries stay listed. PF-20 requires the SOUND request to be independent of visibility, and AC-PF-67 requires 'sound request stays ON' and `amp` >= `floor_eff` for lies 60 to 90 tiles off screen or `away`. But `amp_snd = a_env`, which is driven by `disc`, which is `|slew_pm - u_true|`. PF-34 says the ACTIVE slew of an off-screen ref is not advanced and is re-latched with `hard_start` when next drawn. No rule says what `disc`, `a_env` or `amp_snd` are while the surface is off screen. An implementer could freeze the LEVEL or recompute it from a stale slew. On re-entry `hard_start` would then step `a_env := a_cand`, which is an audible LEVEL step on re-entry and a possible oracle.
findings.fix: Add to PF-34 and D.15: for an off-screen ACTIVE ref, `disc` is taken from the closed-form target (`target_pm - u_true`, not the slew), and `a_env` and `amp_snd` advance on elapsed `present_time` with the same scalar follower as RETURN. State that `hard_start` on re-entry is then a no-op for `amp_snd`. Extend AC-PF-67 to log the LEVEL requests across the off-screen interval and assert no step above AUDIO_LEVEL_STEP_PM on re-entry.

findings.section: Formulas D.11 (a) / Tuning Derived constraints / Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-12; Open Questions OQ-PF-45
findings.finding: Two problems. (1) The reported figure is wrong. The derived-constraints row and AC-PF-12 report 0.0725 at 640x360 k=3 'cap 0, bound against 0.10 holds', and AC-PF-12 'exempts' that rung from the 0.05 margin. But assertion (r) is stated 'after the cap', and after the cap the breathing gleams are removed. The remaining rim plus non-breathing gleams give (353.4 + 120) x 0.291 / 2844 = 0.0484, which is at most 0.05. The exemption is unnecessary and the AC mixes pre-cap and post-cap numbers. This is the previous 'self-referential' finding, only partly cleaned. (2) The cap drops static-pair lies by zoom rung. At 640x360, k=3 and stage 3, with the rim shipped, a housing or glyph lie takes the honest path (filter_draws_dropped) when the player zooms in, and returns when they zoom out. That is a zoom-toggle lie test, and it conflicts with PF-34 and PF-G9 and with PF-15's 'never reduces how a drawn lie leaks'. OQ-PF-45 leaves it to the Pipeline with no deadline.
findings.fix: (1) Restate the rung table as pre-cap 0.0725 and post-cap 0.0484 (<= 0.05, no exemption), and rewrite AC-PF-12: 'THEN dY_region after the cap N_G_REGION(k) is <= FILTER_FLASH_MARGIN at every rung, including 640x360 k 3 (0.0484)'. (2) Make the Pipeline ask binding: the ladder stops at k_auto+1 (or enforces a minimum field of about 320x180 art px) on windows where A_region_min(k) is under 3 000 art px^2. Otherwise define the cap per window size rather than per rung, so that a zoom change never changes which lies are drawn. Record the decision in PF-34.

findings.section: Detailed Rules PF-15 / PF-37 / Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-93; sibling sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md SN-23
findings.finding: Carried from the previous review and still unresolved. The SOUND-drop draw has two owners. Sanity SN-23 (L357) says the drop 'is a pure rng_derive keyed filter.leak/<PlayerId>/<lie_id> (the Filter's stream name, a proposed registry stream)'. The Filter says it uses presentation hash tag 7, and PF-37, X-1 and AC-PF-93 forbid `rng_derive` ('sim-only, KERN D.10, H9'), so an `rng_derive` call from the Filter would fail its own lint. It is dormant because MODE_DROP_PM is 0 at MVP, but the contracts directly contradict each other. This is a G1 case, and the Filter owns the draw.
findings.fix: Conform Sanity to the Filter (G1): replace the sentence in SN-23 with 'the Filter's plausibility drop of the SOUND bit is a PRESENTATION-only hash draw (Perception Filter D.14 tag 7) that touches no RNG stream, counter or ledger field'. Remove the proposed `filter.leak` stream from the registry candidates.

findings.section: Open Questions OQ-PF-38 item 3 / Detailed Rules PF-13; sibling sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md SN-23 legal-kind additions
findings.finding: The zone-edge gate has not been conformed. Sanity's gate (b) rejects a FALSE_* kind only when 'zone-edge distance + m_z exceeds D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000' (400 pm). The reach the Filter can actually deliver is min(400, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s x 1000 / arc_deg). That is 200 pm at L_s = 40 s and 240 deg (D.2 table: D_eff 48 deg), and 400 pm only from 80 s. Zone distances of 200 to 400 pm on a 40 s lie pass Sanity's gate and then miss. The result is `lies_zone_missed` (WARN) on a stage-1 FALSE_OK. The Filter text says Sanity 'reads the Filter's registered constants', but only one constant is read. OQ-PF-38 item 3 also still says 'room in some direction' although gate (a) is now direction-specific.
findings.fix: Have SN-23 (b) use the Filter's reach: `reach_pm(L_s, arc_deg) = min(D_MAX_FRAC_ARC x 1000, GLIDE_REACH_FRAC x GLIDE_RATE_MAX_DEG x L_s x 1000 / arc_deg)`. The Filter confirms the constants and offers `reach_pm` as a pure helper. Fix the 'in some direction' wording in OQ-PF-38 item 3. Add a Filter-side AC that every FALSE_* row of `lie_targets_fixture.json` passes the gate and yields lies_zone_missed 0 at L_s = 40 s.

findings.section: Open Questions OQ-PF-42 / Dependencies bidirectionality; siblings in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view.md and hud-and-suit-layer.md
findings.finding: Fourth consecutive review in which the dependency is not bidirectional. Grep finds no `tremor_weight_pm` and no BREATH anywhere in In-World Instruments or HUD & Suit Layer. Instruments' Perceived field list (L535) has 9 fields against the Filter's 10. Both sibling GDDs still cite `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` 0.6 and 'range 0.5-1.0' (Instruments L396; HUD L256, L1665, L1814 and others), against the Filter and registry value of 0.7 (range 0.7-1.0), which the Filter owns. BREATH is the commonest stage-2 and stage-3 surface mode (glyph, housing, STALE numeral). The creative-director asked last pass for a mandatory epic-gate precondition; a grep finds no 'epic' in the Filter, so it was not made. OQ-PF-42 still says 'required before the sibling GDDs are next edited; this GDD edits none of them', which G6 has made out of date.
findings.fix: Under G6 the siblings' writers apply: (1) Instruments gets a BREATH dispatch row, `tremor_weight_pm` in its Perceived field list (with the blend over TREMOR_BLEND_S), and RM_GLIDE_SCALE 0.7; (2) HUD gets BREATH on HUD glass and RM_GLIDE_SCALE 0.7. In the Filter, add to OQ-PF-42 and the Dependencies section: 'HARD EPIC GATE: no Instruments or HUD story that consumes `perceived()` may enter a sprint until both GDDs carry tremor_weight_pm, BREATH and RM_GLIDE_SCALE 0.7 (confirming consistency-check, patch counts printed)'. Update the Instruments and HUD rows in the I-B table to match.

findings.section: Formulas D.3 (the `s` latch) and the A-interval wording
findings.finding: The text says `s` is latched at the first listed frame and is a function of `direction` and the static record only, but also says that if a record holds more than one alarm interval, A is the one 'closest to u_true at that frame'. That makes `s` depend on the live truth at the latch frame, so it is not restore-exact (hard_start re-latches at a different truth). MVP dials hold one alarm interval, so this is dormant.
findings.fix: Choose A by the same static rule Sanity uses for its dial-room gate (for example the alarm interval nearest the OK-interval midpoint, or the first authored one). Alternatively state that multi-alarm records are ineligible for GLIDE until a rule is written, and add that to the PF-6 lint.

findings.section: Formulas D.6 variables table (L848); Edge Cases E-PF-57; Tuning Knobs vs AC-PF-49(g)
findings.finding: Stale or inconsistent text in this file. (a) D.6's `rm` row still reads 'RM_GLIDE_SCALE 0.6'; the value is 0.7 everywhere else. (b) E-PF-57 lists the assertion 'LEAK_D_FULL_DEG at or below LEAK_EPS_DEG', but the Tuning table and AC-PF-49(g) use 'at or below 2 x LEAK_EPS_DEG'. (c) OQ-PF-42 and the UI Requirements intro say neighbours are 'undesigned or in flight' and the Instruments, HUD and Debug Overlay rows are 'provisional', although they are designed. (d) Game Feel PX-8 and OQ-PF-4 say '5 on the Deck-class machine', where R12 now names RM-DECK.
findings.fix: Change (a) to 0.7. In (b), use the 2x form in E-PF-57. In (c), change the status labels to designed. In (d), write 'on RM-DECK (R12)'.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs: SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM; Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-66c
findings.finding: SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM has a stated safe range of 300 to 800, but Audio D.19 R-j fails for values under 461 at HAL_FLOOR_DB -31, a DIAGNOSTIC. So 300 to 460 is not a safe range. AC-PF-66c says 'S3 is NONE or exactly at the follower's elapsed-time position' without giving the expected value, so the oracle is not computable.
findings.fix: Narrow the range to 461 to 800 (or label 300 to 460 'allowed only with Audio logging the R-j diagnostic'). Rewrite AC-PF-66c: 'GIVEN end_run passes at t_e while away is true and the surface is off screen for 50 s WHEN it is next drawn at t_d THEN displayed_pm equals the live truth if (t_d - t_e) x R_ret >= the gap at t_e, otherwise it is within one frame of u_true +/- (gap_end - R_ret x (t_d - t_e)); amp_snd equals max(0, amp_end - R_AMP x (t_d - t_e)); S3 is RETURN or NONE accordingly and is never ONSET or HOLD.'

findings.section: Detailed Rules PF-20 / PF-34 / D.15; Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-67
findings.finding: Underspecified now that away entries stay listed. PF-20 requires the SOUND request to be independent of visibility, and AC-PF-67 requires 'sound request stays ON' and `amp` >= `floor_eff` for lies 60 to 90 tiles off screen or `away`. But `amp_snd = a_env`, which is driven by `disc`, which is `|slew_pm - u_true|`. PF-34 says the ACTIVE slew of an off-screen ref is not advanced and is re-latched with `hard_start` when next drawn. No rule says what `disc`, `a_env` or `amp_snd` are while the surface is off screen. An implementer could freeze the LEVEL or recompute it from a stale slew. On re-entry `hard_start` would then step `a_env := a_cand`, which is an audible LEVEL step on re-entry and a possible oracle.
findings.fix: Add to PF-34 and D.15: for an off-screen ACTIVE ref, `disc` is taken from the closed-form target (`target_pm - u_true`, not the slew), and `a_env` and `amp_snd` advance on elapsed `present_time` with the same scalar follower as RETURN. State that `hard_start` on re-entry is then a no-op for `amp_snd`. Extend AC-PF-67 to log the LEVEL requests across the off-screen interval and assert no step above AUDIO_LEVEL_STEP_PM on re-entry.

findings.section: Formulas D.11 (a) / Tuning Derived constraints / Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-12; Open Questions OQ-PF-45
findings.finding: Two problems. (1) The reported figure is wrong. The derived-constraints row and AC-PF-12 report 0.0725 at 640x360 k=3 'cap 0, bound against 0.10 holds', and AC-PF-12 'exempts' that rung from the 0.05 margin. But assertion (r) is stated 'after the cap', and after the cap the breathing gleams are removed. The remaining rim plus non-breathing gleams give (353.4 + 120) x 0.291 / 2844 = 0.0484, which is at most 0.05. The exemption is unnecessary and the AC mixes pre-cap and post-cap numbers. This is the previous 'self-referential' finding, only partly cleaned. (2) The cap drops static-pair lies by zoom rung. At 640x360, k=3 and stage 3, with the rim shipped, a housing or glyph lie takes the honest path (filter_draws_dropped) when the player zooms in, and returns when they zoom out. findings.section: Detailed Rules PF-15 / PF-37 / Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-93; sibling sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md SN-23

findings.section: Open Questions OQ-PF-38 item 3 / Detailed Rules PF-13; sibling sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md SN-23 legal-kind additions

findings.section: Formulas D.3 (the `s` latch) and the A-interval wording

findings.section: Tuning Knobs: SOUND_BREATH_FLOOR_PM; Acceptance Criteria AC-PF-66c
